Once upon a time there was a careless boy called Joe. One day, Joe wanted to read a book. He went to the store, but he forgot to bring some gas money. He had no way to get back home, so he asked his friend to help him.

But Joe's friend was very careless too. He told him "I won't give you any gas money, so you have to walk". Joe felt sad and unhappy. He slowly walked back home.

On the way home, he saw some other children playing around. But none of their parents were around to watch them. He realized how careless he and his friend had been and he knew he had to be more careful in future.

Finally Joe made it home. He was relieved and glad to be back. He knew his lesson for the day - Always be careful, think first, and always bring some money with you.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was very happy and curious. She wanted to know about everything and asked lots of questions.

One day, Daisy followed her teacher outside. The teacher showed her a very pretty flower. Daisy thought it was so attractive.

The teacher taught Daisy how to take care of the flower. Every day, Daisy came out and watered it with her watering can.

Soon the flower was growing big, with lots of petals. Daisy was very excited that she'd taken care of the flower, and made it so happy.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a fish. The fish was very charming, and he thought he'd go for a swim.

The fish swam in and out of the coral, and he saw so many colors, shapes and sizes. He thought it was so fun!

As he swam around, the fish saw a little bird. The bird said â€œHi! What are you doing here?â€

The fish said â€œI am just swimming and looking for things to eat.â€

The bird said â€œThatâ€™s so wonderful! Maybe we could be friends!â€

The fish was so happy! He said â€œYES! Letâ€™s be friends!â€

So, the fish and the bird were best friends and they swam and flew around the ocean together, having a lot of fun. They thought they would be friends forever.

One day, a lawyer went to the park. He was glad because it was sunny. He saw a little girl with a red ball. The girl was sad because her ball was stuck in a tree.

The lawyer said, "I can help you." He took a long stick and got the ball out of the tree. The girl was so happy. She said, "Thank you!"

The lawyer was glad he could help. He said, "You're welcome!" The girl and the lawyer played with the ball. They had a fun day at the park.

Andy and Jane were playing in the living room. Suddenly, Andy heard a noise coming from behind the curtain. He shouted "What is that?" Jane was scared and ran away. Andy didn't know what to do, so he decided to take a peek. He bravely opened the curtain and his heart felt hurt when he saw a mouse. He didn't know how to deal with this and he started to shout and scream. Jane, who had been hiding, came back to help him and she shouted too, which scared the mouse away. Andy and Jane hugged each other and they were relieved that there was no more conflict.

Once upon a time, there was a big river where a lot of animals lived. One day, a brilliant alligator appeared and all the other animals were afraid of him. They thought he might be mean and eat them all up. But then, a little monkey came along and said, "Let's guess what the alligator wants to do!" So they all guessed and the monkey said, "Maybe he just wants to be our friend!" And guess what? The alligator was friendly and liked to play with all the other animals in the river. From that day on, they all had fun together and the brilliant alligator was no longer scary.

Once upon a time, a small cube lived in a tight box. The cube was sad because it could not move or play with its friends. One day, a kind girl named Lily found the box and opened it.

"Hello, little cube," said Lily. "Why are you so sad?" The cube told Lily that it was sad because it could not move or play. Lily wanted to help and comfort the cube. So, she took the cube out of the tight box and held it in her hands.

Now, the cube could move and play with its friends. The cube was very happy and thanked Lily. "Thank you, Lily, for making me happy!" From that day on, the cube and Lily became best friends, and they played together every day.

Once there was an old barn in a quiet meadow. Every day the animals would come out to play, and the barn was home to an old horse. The horse would gently neigh and the other animals would talk with him.

One day, the animals noticed something strange. A little girl came and stood outside the barn. She had a basket of food and some carrots. She was very gentle and the animals were curious.

The horse walked up to the girl. He softly pushed his muzzle against her hand and she smiled. She whispered something in the horse's ear.

The horse broke into a trot and the animals followed behind him. He ran up to the little girl and she laughed. She put the carrots in his mane and gave him a hug.

The animals were so happy. Even the chickens were chirping. The old horse talked to the girl, and she listened to all the stories he wanted to tell. 

The little girl left after giving the animals food and love. The animals waved goodbye and the old horse said "Thank You" in a gentle neigh.

Lily and Tom were playing in the garden. They had a big bucket of water and some cups. They wanted to soak each other and have fun.

"Tom, I will soak you first!" Lily said. She filled her cup with water and threw it at Tom. But Tom was fast and dodged the water. He laughed and said, "You missed me, Lily!"

Lily was angry. She filled her cup again and ran after Tom. Tom ran to the tree and climbed to the top. He thought he was safe there. He looked down at Lily and said, "You can't soak me now, Lily! I am on the top of the tree!"

Lily was not ignorant. She knew how to soak Tom. She took the bucket and poured all the water on the tree. The water dripped down and soaked Tom. He was wet and cold. He said, "Lily, that's not fair! You soaked me too much!"

Lily smiled and said, "I soaked you, Tom! I soaked you good!" She climbed the tree and hugged Tom. They were both wet and happy. They played some more and then went inside to change their clothes.

Once there was a lion who liked lollipops very much. He was different to other lions as he loved the sweet taste of lollipops.

Every day, he would go to the lollipop forest to find the biggest and tastiest lollipops. He made sure to get there before everyone else!

One day, something unusual happened. He found the biggest and yummiest lollipop ever! It was so big and sweet, he just had to roar with happiness.

He quickly grabbed the lollipop and ran away. The other animals were so surprised, they were all amazed at how the lion had found such an unusual lollipop.

The lion happily enjoyed his sweet lollipop and made sure he visited the lollipop forest again the next day.

One day, a little ball named Bounce went to the park. Bounce loved to jump up and down. Bounce saw a big wrap on a bench. The wrap was sad because it felt uncomfortable.

Bounce asked the wrap, "Why are you sad?" The wrap said, "I am uncomfortable because I am too big and heavy. I want to be like you and jump up and down."

Bounce thought for a moment and said, "Let's play a game. I will jump on you and make you feel better." The wrap agreed and Bounce started to jump on the wrap. The wrap felt less uncomfortable.

Suddenly, a strong wind came and blew the wrap away. Bounce was sad because he lost his new friend. Bounce decided to search for the wrap. He jumped high and low, looking everywhere.

Finally, Bounce found the wrap stuck in a tree. Bounce jumped high and helped the wrap get down. They were both happy again. From that day on, Bounce and the wrap played together every day and became best friends.

Tim and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with cars and balls and blocks. One day, they found a big box in the garage. It was full of shiny things. They opened the box and saw many things they did not know.

"What is this?" Tim asked, holding a round thing with a hole in the middle.

"I don't know. It looks like a green donut," Sam said.

"Can we eat it?" Tim wondered.

"Let's try," Sam said.

They each took a green donut and put it in their mouths. They made a face. It was not sweet. It was bitter and salty. They spit it out.

"Yuck! This is not a donut. This is a bad thing," Tim said.

"Maybe it is an olive," Sam said. He had heard his mom say that word before.

"An olive? What is an olive?" Tim asked.

"I don't know. But I don't like it," Sam said.

They threw the olives away and looked for something else in the box. They saw a shiny thing that looked like a star. It had many colors and sparkles.

"Wow! Look at this!" Tim said, grabbing the star.

"It is brilliant!" Sam said, admiring the star.

"Can we play with it?" Tim asked.

"Sure. Let's spin it and see what happens," Sam said.

They spun the star and watched it shine. It was very pretty. They spun it faster and faster. They did not see the wire that was attached to the star. The wire was connected to a plug in the wall. The plug was old and broken.

Suddenly, there was a loud noise and a flash of light. The star exploded. The wire sparked. The box caught fire. Tim and Sam screamed. They dropped the star and ran out of the garage. They saw smoke and flames. They were scared and hurt. They cried for help.

Their mom and dad heard them and came running. They saw the fire and called the firemen. They hugged Tim and Sam and took them to the hospital. They were very angry and sad.

Tim and Sam learned a hard lesson. They should not play with things they do not know. They should not spin stars. They should not eat olives. They should listen to their mom and dad. They should be careful and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat grapes, especially the purple ones. One day, she saw a grape on the ground and picked it up. She wondered if it was still good to eat.

Lily tried the grape and it was delicious! She was so happy that she found a yummy grape. But then, she dropped the grape and it rolled away. Lily searched and searched for the grape, but it was persistent in hiding from her.

Finally, Lily found the grape under a chair. She was so happy to find it again and ate it right away. From then on, Lily always made sure to hold onto her grapes tightly so they wouldn't roll away again.

The sun was shining brightly, so Mommy took Charlie to the pond. He was so excited! Charlie started splashing in the water with his hands. He was having so much fun! Then Daddy came over with a net. He scooped it through the water and pulled it up. There were some little fish inside. He said â€œthese fish are all mine!â€ Charlie was so excited, he splashed even more. Even Mommy was getting wet! Charlie had a great day at the pond, splashing and playing with the fish in the water.

Once there was a beautiful princess named Daisy. Daisy loved her family and had a very strong urge to marry. One day, Daisy's mother told her she ought to marry very soon. She was excited, but worried.

Daisy went outside to her favourite spot. While she was thinking, a rude man came to her. He began asking her to marry him. Daisy was scared; she knew he was not a nice person. She didn't like how he talked and quickly ran away.

The next day, Daisy's mother realised that the rude man had been a prince. He had come to her spot because he had heard Daisy wanted to marry. Daisy was very sad. She had wanted to marry, but not to someone so rude.

The day of Daisy's wedding came. When the doors opened, Daisy's heart skipped a beat. Standing in the doorway was the same prince from the day before. He had come to propose with all of his respect, and Daisy was finally able to marry the prince she had always wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot liked to play and run all day. One day, Spot saw a big ball in the yard. He wanted to play with it, but he knew it was not his ball. Spot thought it would be fun, so he took the ball anyway.

Spot played with the ball all day. He did not know that he was making trouble. The ball belonged to his friend, Sam the cat. Sam was sad because he could not find his ball to complete his game. When Sam saw Spot with his ball, he felt very sorry.

Spot saw that Sam was sad and knew he made trouble. He felt sorry too. Spot gave the ball back to Sam and said sorry. They played together with the ball and had a great day. From that day on, Spot learned to share and not take things that were not his.

Sammy slowly walked up to the university. It was such a colorful place. He couldn't help but be captivated by it. But as he looked up he spotted an old man on a bench. He got a little scared and wanted to run back home. The old man noticed him and smiled.

"Hi Sammy," he said. "I'm an old professor here at the university. What can I do for you today?"

Sammy cautiously nodded. He was still a little scared but he wanted to stay and hear what the old man had to say.

"I'm here to give you an important task," the old man said. "This task will be hard and it won't be easy. But if you do it, you'll be very proud of yourself. Are you up for it?"

Sammy hesitated for a moment. Then he firmly nodded. He was ready for this challenge! He didn't know what it was yet but he knew it was going to be an amazing experience. 

The old man smiled and started to explain how it was Sammy's job to protect the university from danger. He told Sammy he had to be brave and vigilant. With a foreboding look in his eyes, the old man said, "This task won't be easy, but I have faith in you, Sammy. I know you can do it."

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved puzzles. She loved the feeling of putting them together. One day she had a big plan. She was going to put together a light puzzle.

She took some time to work on it. Every now and then she needed help from her mommy. She asked questions like, â€œDoes this piece go here?â€ and â€œHow do I make this part fit?â€

Everyday she would take small breaks to show her progress. Still, she kept working and trying.

Finally, after lots of hard work, she finished her puzzle. She screamed â€œI did it! I finished my puzzle!â€

Her mommy, who was standing nearby, smiled. â€œI knew you could do it!â€

The girl was so proud, and the puzzle glowed a bright happy light. It was so pretty that she wanted to show it to everyone.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Christopher who was very thoughtful. He loved to draw and design things. One day Christopher saw a big blackboard in the park.

He thought it would be fun to design something on it. He took out his markers and drew a happy lion with a colourful mane. He also drew a rainbow and some trees. It was a very cheerful design. 

Christopher showed his design to some other children in the park. They were all very impressed and thought it was fantastic. 

Everyone loved what Christopher had designed on the blackboard. It really brightened up the park. 

From then on, Christopher would come to the park every day to design something new and creative to share with the other children.

Once upon a time there was a charming little port. All the boats would come in for docking and refueling before going off to explore new lands. One day a young sailor named Jack set off on a grand adventure, with one mission: to rescue his beloved sailboat from a distant island.

Jack was so determined to reach his goal, but as he ventured farther out to sea, he began to fear he would never get there in time. Suddenly, a wave washed up onto the deck, revealing a tiny island in the distance. Without hesitation, Jack steered his boat toward the small port.

At the charming port, Jack was able to refuel his boat and find supplies for his rescue mission. He said his goodbyes to the friendly locals and sailed off into the horizon. Finally, after days of sailing, Jack arrived at his destination â€” the island where his beloved sailboat was stranded.

Jack set out to explore the island, until he discovered his sailboat, just as he had left it. With great joy he was able to rescue his boat from the island and make his voyage back home. What an adventurer Jack had been!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy went on a walk with his family. While they were walking, Timmy observed a little bird in a tree. He pointed and said, "Look, I spot a bird!" His family stopped to look and they saw the bird too. Timmy was so happy that he could observe the bird and share it with his family. They continued their walk and Timmy couldn't wait to spot more animals along the way.

One day, Tom and Sally went for a walk. Tom saw something sparkly on the ground. He went over to mark it. Sally asked, "What is it?" Tom replied, "I do not know. Let's see how much weight it has."

They picked the sparkly thing up. It felt quite heavy. Sally said, "I think it is the key to something!" Tom was alert and quickly looked around but he did not spot anything.

They put the key in Tom's pocket. They walked away and suddenly noticed a chest. It was standing there, all alone. They were excited and ran over. Tom took the key out and opened the chest.

Inside, they found some candy and a funny toy! They were so happy and quickly thanked the key for leading them to this surprise.

Mum and her three-year-old daughter were travelling to their new home. As soon as they arrived, the little girl jumped out of the car and ran to explore her new house. She ran up and down the stairs, feeling wild and free. 

Mum followed, struggling with all the bags. "Honey, can you help me unpack these bags?"

The little girl stopped mid-run and said "Yes, Mum!" 

She helped her Mum unpack the bags, then said "Can I play on the stairs now?"

Mum smiled and said "Yes, off you go!" 

The little girl clapped her hands and ran up the stairs, feeling wild and free. She jumped, twirled and ran up and down the stairs until it was time for dinner. 

Mum smiled and said "Time to come down now, it's dinner time!" 

The little girl came running down the stairs and gave Mum a big hug. She said "Thank you for the wild adventure on the stairs." 

Mum smiled and said, "You're welcome sweetheart."

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in the park. They liked to run, jump, slide and swing. But they did not like to share. They always wanted the same toy, the same snack, the same seat. They always fought and cried.

One day, they saw a big statue in the park. It was a statue of a lion and a mouse. The lion had a thorn in his paw and the mouse was helping him. The twins were curious and went closer. They saw a sign that said: "The Lion and the Mouse. A fable by Aesop. The moral is: A kindness is never wasted."

"What is a fable?" asked Tim.

"What is a moral?" asked Kim.

A lady who was sitting on a bench nearby heard them and smiled. She said: "A fable is a story that teaches a lesson. A moral is the lesson that the story teaches. Do you want me to tell you the story of the lion and the mouse?"

The twins nodded and sat down next to the lady. She told them how the lion was the king of the jungle, but he was also very proud and lazy. He did not care about the other animals and he did not listen to anyone. One day, he was sleeping under a tree when a mouse ran over his nose. The lion woke up and was very angry. He caught the mouse and said: "How dare you disturb me? I will eat you for breakfast!"

The mouse was very scared and said: "Please, Mr. Lion, spare me. I did not mean to bother you. I was just looking for food. If you let me go, I will be grateful and I will help you someday."

The lion laughed and said: "You? Help me? How can a tiny mouse help a mighty lion? You are too weak and small. But I am feeling generous today, so I will let you go. But don't ever come near me again."

The mouse thanked the lion and ran away. The lion went back to sleep.

A few days later, the lion was walking in the forest when he stepped on a sharp thorn. The thorn pierced his paw and made him bleed. The lion roared in pain and tried to pull out the thorn, but he could not reach it. He was in trouble and he needed help.

The mouse heard the lion's roar and recognized his voice. He remembered how the lion had spared his life and he decided to help him. He ran to the lion and said: "Mr. Lion, what is wrong? Can I help you?"

The lion was surprised and ashamed to see the mouse. He said: "Oh, it's you. I have a thorn in my paw and it hurts a lot. But you can't help me. You are too weak and small."

The mouse said: "Don't say that, Mr. Lion. You may be big and strong, but I am smart and brave. Let me see your paw. Maybe I can pull out the thorn."

The lion was doubtful, but he was also desperate. He said: "All right, try it. But be careful. Don't hurt me more."

The mouse climbed on the lion's paw and saw the thorn. He used his teeth and his claws and he pulled out the thorn. The lion felt a relief and thanked the mouse. He said: "You are amazing, little mouse. You have saved me. You have proved that you can help me. I was wrong to laugh at you and to be proud and lazy. I am sorry. Can you forgive me?"

The mouse said: "Of course, I forgive you, Mr. Lion. You have also proved that you can be kind and grateful. I am glad that we are friends. The moral is: A kindness is never wasted."

The twins listened to the story and learned the moral. They looked at each other and said: "We are sorry for fighting and crying. We should be kind and share. We should not be proud and lazy. We should be friends."

The lady smiled and said: "That's right, Tim and Kim. You have learned a valuable lesson. Now, go and play and have fun. And remember: A kindness is never wasted."

Lily and Ben were twins, but they were very different. Lily liked to play with dolls and draw pictures. Ben liked to play with cars and build blocks. One day, they had to share a tray of cookies that their mom made for them.

"Let's pray first," Lily said. She closed her eyes and folded her hands. "Thank you, God, for the cookies and for mom and dad and for Ben."

Ben rolled his eyes. He did not like to pray. He wanted to eat the cookies right away. He opened his eyes and reached for the tray.

"Hey, stop!" Lily said. She opened her eyes and saw Ben grabbing a cookie. "That's not fair! You have to pray first!"

"No, I don't!" Ben said. He bit the cookie and smiled. "Mmm, yummy!"

Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to share the cookies with Ben, but he did not care. She started to cry.

Mom heard Lily crying and came to see what was wrong. She saw the tray of cookies and Ben's crumbs on his mouth.

"What happened here?" Mom asked.

"Lily wanted me to pray, but I didn't want to," Ben said.

"Lily, why did you want Ben to pray?" Mom asked.

"Because it's good to thank God for what we have," Lily said.

Mom nodded. She understood how Lily felt. She also understood how Ben felt. She loved them both, even though they were different.

"Ben, I'm glad you like the cookies, but you should respect Lily's choice to pray. Praying is a way of talking to God and showing gratitude. You don't have to pray if you don't want to, but you should wait for Lily to finish before you take a cookie," Mom said.

"Sorry, Lily," Ben said. He felt a little sorry for making Lily cry.

"Lily, I'm proud of you for praying, but you should respect Ben's choice not to pray. Not everyone believes in God or prays the same way. You can pray for yourself and for Ben, but you can't force him to pray with you," Mom said.

"Sorry, Ben," Lily said. She felt a little sorry for being angry at Ben.

Mom smiled. She hugged them both and gave them each another cookie.

"Can we still play together?" Ben asked.

"Of course we can," Lily said.

They ate their cookies and then played with their toys. They were different, but they were still twins. And they still loved each other.

One day, a panda was walking quickly down the street. Suddenly, it heard loud music! The panda rushed to the sound to discover a big celebration. 

Two children were dancing and playing around. The panda said, "What are you celebrating?"

The children replied, "Today is a special day! We are celebrating!" The panda smiled and joined in the celebration.

Everyone laughed and had a great time. Afterward, the panda thanked the children for a wonderful day. The panda waved goodbye as it ran off down the street, quickly. 

The children watched it go, happy to have celebrated with the panda.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his blocks. He would build towers and castles all day long. Timmy was very creative with his blocks.

One day, Timmy's mom called him for lunch. Timmy was so excited to eat his favorite sandwich. But when he went back to his room to play with his blocks, they were gone! Timmy looked everywhere, but they had disappeared.

Timmy was sad, but he didn't give up. He used his creative mind to think of a way to find his blocks. Suddenly, he remembered that he had let his friend borrow them. Timmy went to his friend's house and there they were - his blocks! Timmy was so happy to have his blocks back and he knew he would never let them disappear again.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters. Their names were Jane and Marie. Jane was three years old and Marie was five years old. 

One day Marie said to Jane, "Let's play a game". Jane was excited and said, "Yes, what will we play?" Marie said, "Let's pretend that we have a pot full of healthy rice". Jane replied, "How do we do that?" Marie said,  "We just have to believe".

Jane and Marie smiled and immediately started to imagine that there was a pot full of healthy rice. They both said, "We believe there is a pot full of healthy rice". 

Suddenly, Jane heard a sound. She looked around the room and saw the pot of healthy rice she and her sister had believed in. Jane and Marie both were amazed and hugged each other, excited for their game. They laughed and enjoyed their pot of healthy rice for days and days!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with clay. One day, he made a long clay snake. He was very proud of his snake. He showed it to his friend, Sam.

Sam said, "I can make a longer snake." Tim and Sam had a serious face. They both wanted to win. They started to stretch their clay snakes. They pulled and pulled, making the snakes longer and longer.

But then, both snakes broke! Tim and Sam looked at their broken snakes. They felt sad. Tim said, "Let's work together." They put the two pieces together and made a new, long snake. They were both happy and played together all day.

Once there was a girl called Amy. She was three years old and she had a perfect phone which made her very happy.

One night, Amy had to go to bed. But she didn't want to, she wanted to play with her phone! She begged, "Please Mum, can I stay up for just a few more minutes?"

But her mum said no. "Amy, No! You must sleep now."

Amy cried and begged again, but her mum was firm. She put the phone away and tucked Amy in.

Suddenly, there came a bright light from Amy's room! It was coming from her phone! She quickly grabbed it and looked in wonder. On the phone was a beautiful game, perfect and exciting.

Amy wanted to play. She tried to get up, but her Mum said,"No!" She stayed in bed and the bright phone light faded away.

Amy was disappointed, but she knew it was the right thing to do. She closed her eyes and went to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sally. Sally was very silly and liked to play games. One day, her mother told her it was time to go to bed. But Sally was too busy playing and did not want to go. 

Her mother warned her not to stay up too late. Sally kept ignoring her. Finally, her mother said, "If you don't go to bed now, I will have to punish you!"

Sally thought about it for a moment and said, "But I want a strawberry!"

Her mother replied, "No, no strawberries now! Go to bed or you will have to be punished!"

Sally knew her mother meant it. She got up and said, "OK, I'm going to bed."

And that's the end of the story! Sometimes, it's important to listen to our parents, even if it seems silly.

Once there were two friends, Anna and Tim. Anna was tall and Tim was small. But what they had in common was their love for their team. Every day they would cheer for their team to win the game.

One day, Tim fell down and scraped his knee. Anna hugged him tight and cheered him up. She said: "We will keep cheering for our team together!"

After that, they smiled and hugged each other to show they were friends. And they cheered on their team even louder.

Anna and Tim had so much fun that day, and they continued to cheer on their team together. Together, they were a great team!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Jill. One day, Jill's mommy wanted to give her a bath. She brought Jill to the bathroom and put her in the bathtub. 

Jill wasn't used to bathing, but her mommy wanted to encourage her to try. She said, "You can do it, Jill! Can you use the washcloth to make bubbles?" 

Jill was scared, so she said no. But her mommy kept encouraging her. She said, "It's okay, sweetheart. I'm here. I'll help you." 

Jill felt a little better. So she put the washcloth in the water and made a lot of pale bubbles. She even splashed around and laughed. 

At the end of the bath, Jill felt proud of herself. She had done something new and exciting. And her mommy was so proud of her too.

Anna liked to go to the park with her mom and dad. She liked to see the ducks and the swans in the pond. She liked to feed them bread and watch them swim.

One day, she saw a swan that was not lively. It was lying on the grass and did not move. Anna felt sad for the swan. She asked her mom and dad what was wrong with it.

Her mom and dad said the swan was hurt. It had a hook in its wing. The hook was from a fisher who was not careful. They said they would try to fix the swan and make it better.

They called a helper who worked with animals. The helper came with a big net and a box. He was gentle with the swan. He took the hook out of its wing and put some cream on it. He put the swan in the box and said he would take it to a safe place.

Anna was happy that the helper would fix the swan. She hoped the swan would be lively again soon. She said goodbye to the swan and thanked the helper. She gave the swan a kiss and a hug. She said she would come back to the park and look for the swan when it was well.

One day, a boy called Jack had a really cool pistol. He loved playing with it in the garden. He ran around, jumped and waved his pistol in the air. 

Suddenly his friend Lilly came over. "What's that?" she asked. Jack proudly held up his pistol. "It's my new pistol," he said. "It's so cool!"

Lilly gasped. "I love it! It looks like so much fun. Can I have a go?"

Jack smiled and said, "Yes! Let's play together." He showed Lilly how to hold the pistol and he showed her how to jump while shooting. Lilly loved it, while Jack had even more fun showing her.

At the end of their game, Lilly held up the pistol and said, "This is the coolest pistol ever!" Jack grinned and said, "I know - it's mine!"

Once there was a little girl. Every year she would go to the park and drop her food in the park for the birds to eat. She was so unselfish and kind to the birds. 

One day, a naughty boy saw her. He thought it was not fair that she was so unselfish and wanted to keep the food for himself. He followed her to the park and started dropping his food too. 

The little girl was very surprised. She asked the naughty boy why he was dropping his food. He wouldn't answer and just continued to drop the food. 

The little girl quickly realized that the naughty boy was very selfish. She said, "You should share your food with the birds. That is the kind thing to do." 

The naughty boy then realized that it was not nice to be selfish, and he started to share his food with the birds too. The birds were so happy! From that day on, the little girl and the naughty boy both dropped their food in the park every year so that the birds could eat.

Once there was a little girl called Amy. She was three years old. She had one little toy - it was her favourite. One day she was playing with it and she wanted to throw it up into the air. She picked it up by the handle and threw it into the air. 

But when the toy came down, it got stuck in a tree! Amy was so confused. She didn't know what to do. She looked around and around but she couldn't see the toy anywhere. 

Suddenly the wind started to blow and the toy fell out of the tree. Amy was so happy! She ran to get it, grabbed the handle and hugged her toy close.

Amy was no longer confused - she was very happy and she threw her toy up into the air again and again.

Once upon a time there was a thin sack. One day, the sack was walking in the woods when it saw a pie on the ground. The sack was so hungry, it wanted to eat the pie.

The sack asked, "Can I eat this pie?"

Suddenly, a voice came from the sky. 

"Do not eat, sack," the voice said.

The sack was confused. Why not eat it?

The voice said, "It's not yours and if you eat it, the other animals won't have anything to eat. You should share so everyone can enjoy it."

The sack thought carefully and realized the voice was right. It did not eat the pie, but took it to a nearby stream and placed it down.

The sack looked around to make sure no one was there. Then it broke up the pie into small pieces and spread it all around the stream.

Soon, lots of animals came to the stream and ate the pie. Everyone was happy, including the thin sack.

The moral of the story is that sharing is caring. Nobody should take something that doesn't belong to them, but instead should think of others and share with them.

The little boy had a uniform that was too big for him. His mom saw how sad he was, so she hugged him and said, "It's okay sweetie, don't feel sorry." He felt better, but still not quite ready to put his uniform on. 

His mom told him, "The sun is rising, and you have to get ready for school." He looked outside, and she was right; the sun was rising slowly in the sky. He knew he had to get ready for school, so he said, "Yes mommy, I understand." 

He put his uniform on, but it still felt too big. So his mom got out the sewing machine and said, "Don't worry, I'll make it fit you better." She worked on his uniform while he watched, and then he put it back on. He saw how it fit him much better than before; he felt happy and ready to go to school.

He thanked his mom and gave her a big hug. Then he quickly ran outside and watched the sun rise above the horizon. He was so excited for another day of school, and he knew he could do it in his new uniform.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved to go exploring in her garden, searching for little treasures. One day as she skipped around, she stopped to look in the garden pond. Suddenly, she spotted something glinting in the water. She reached her hand in and pulled out a thick coin. She was so excited she ran straight in to show her mom.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lonely dog named Max. Max did not have any friends to play with. One day, Max went on a walk to search for new friends.

While Max was searching, the ground started to shake. It was an earthquake! Max was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He ran to find a safe place to hide.

After the earthquake, Max saw a little girl who was also scared. He went to her and they became friends. They were not lonely anymore. They played together and were happy. And that is how Max found a friend after the earthquake.

Once there was a mommy and a baby. Mommy wanted to borrow something from Grandma. She asked Grandma if she could borrow a cushion. Grandma said yes, but only if she was careful. The cushion was very fragile. 

So Mommy took the fragile cushion home. She put it on the couch so the baby could sit on it. The baby was very happy because the cushion was so soft and squishy. 

The next day Mommy took the cushion to Grandma's house. Grandma thanked Mommy for taking such good care of the cushion. Mommy said she was happy to borrow it and thanked Grandma for being so kind. 

The Baby and Mommy waved goodbye and headed home. They were both happy to be reunited with Grandma and the special cushion.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She lived in a very big house all alone. She always felt very lonely. 

One day, Lucy wanted to have dinner. She went to the kitchen, opened the cupboard and saw that it was empty.

"Oh no!" she said to herself. "I'm very hungry, but I don't have anything to eat."

Then, she had an idea. She went outside and started walking around. After a while she saw an old man. He was sitting on the street corner and he was smiling. 

Lucy went up to him and asked, "Excuse me, can you help me?"

"Yes, of course," the old man said. "What do you need?"

"I'm very hungry. Can I get some rice?" Lucy asked.

"Yes, of course. Here you go," the old man said. He took out a big bag of rice, gave it to Lucy and said, "It's all yours. I hope it helps."

Lucy was so happy, she thanked the man and went home. 

When she got home, she cooked the rice and had dinner. She felt much better and was no longer lonely. Lucy thanked the old man again. From then on, she was never hungry and she was never alone.

Once upon a time, there was a smart girl named Liza. She loved to sing and was always interested in fashion. Every morning Liza woke up and sang a happy little song. Her song was always noticed by the neighborhood birds, which would come and join in with their own chirps. 

One day, Liza had an idea. She decided to make her own fashion show. She carefully selected her best outfits and accessories, and began preparing for the fashion show. She sang a happy little song as she got ready.

Finally the day of the fashion show arrived. Everyone was very excited. Liza walked out onto the stage, wearing her finest outfit. The crowd cheered loudly as she twirled around showing them her pretty dress. She finished her routine with a final flourish and sang a beautiful song.

The crowd was delighted. Liza had put on a truly amazing show. She was very smart, indeed. From that day on, Liza and her pretty dress became a part of the town's fashionable landscape. And her songs were often heard echoing in the streets.

Once upon a time, there was a good boy named Timmy. Timmy always listened to his mommy and daddy. He was obedient. 

One day, Timmy's mommy gave him a present. It was a toy car. Timmy loved his present so much that he played with it all day long. 

But then, it was time for Timmy to go to bed. Before he went to sleep, his mommy told him to wash his hands and face. Timmy went to the bathroom and washed his hands and face very well. 

After he finished washing, Timmy went to bed with his present next to him. He fell asleep with a big smile on his face. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a team of sleepy workers. Every day they all went to sleep. One morning, the leader of the team woke them all up. He was rude and shouted "Wake up!" The team all jumped out of bed. They all got dressed and started to work.

They went around doing their jobs. They worked hard and were very tired, but the leader wouldn't let them rest. He kept ordering them to work. The team worked until dark and the leader told them to keep going.

That night, the team was so tired that they fell asleep standing up. They were so tired that even the rude leader wanted to rest. He gave them all a break and said "Go to bed now". So everyone went to bed early that night.

The next morning, the leader said "Wake up! It's time to go to work!" The team was glad they got to sleep and they worked really hard all day. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved music and wanted to play the violin. Her mommy and daddy promised to buy her one. 

One day, they went to a music store and saw a shiny, brown violin. Lily was so happy! She tried to play it, but it made a screeching sound. Her mommy and daddy said they would answer her prayers and get her lessons.

After a few weeks of practice, Lily played a beautiful song on her violin. Her mommy and daddy were so proud! They celebrated with a spicy dinner. Lily realized that practicing and patience paid off.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sam. She was three years old and very unique; she loved to wear what made her happy. 

One day, Sam asked her mum, "Where can I get the new dress I want?"

Her mum smiled and said, "Let's go to the mill and see if we can find it."

So off they went, but when they got there they didn't find what they were looking for.

Instead, Sam noticed a beautiful fabric with bright colours. Her mum said, "What a lovely material, why don't you make something special with it?"

And that's exactly what Sam did. She took the fabric home and made herself a unique dress. 

Sam wore it proudly and was so happy. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sweets and candies. One day, she went to the candy store with her mom.

Lily looked at all the candies and chocolates with different colors and shapes. Her mom suggested that she should try a candy with a bumpy texture. Lily was not sure, but her mom said it might be tasty.

Lily tried the candy and it was delicious! She loved the bumpy texture and the tasty flavor. She thanked her mom for suggesting it to her. From that day on, Lily always tried new candies with different textures and flavors.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Frisky. Frisky was a clumsy bird, but she always wanted to soar like the other birds. 

One day, she watched the other birds and said, "I want to soar too!" 

The birds told her that it was easy. All she had to do was spread her little wings and let them flutter in the wind. 

Frisky tried this, but even after a lot of flapping, she couldn't soar. But then one of the birds said, "Just stop flapping and let the wind do the work!" 

So Frisky opened her wings wide and felt the motion of the wind all around her. She smiled and after a few moments, she was soaring up high. She was so happy that she never wanted to come down. 

From then on, every day Frisky would spread her wings and soar into the sky. She loved the feeling of being free. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a bunny named Ben. Ben was going on a trip to visit his friends and he needed to pack a lot of things.

He started with his clothes. He grabbed a few shirts and put them in his bag. He also packed a pair of pants and two pairs of shoes.

Next, Ben added some snacks. He put a few carrots, apples, and berries in a small container. He even added a few nuts and dried fruits.

Finally, Ben grabbed a big knob and put it in his bag. It was hard and heavy, but he knew he needed it for his trip.

Just when he was about to close his bag, Ben's mommy called him.

"Ben, don't forget to bring your sweater", she said.

"Yes, Mommy", replied Ben.

He quickly packed his sweater and zipped up his bag. Off he went, with a big smile on his face, ready to start his trip.

Billy was a brave kid. He always wanted to explore, so one day he walked into an ancient forest. Suddenly, he heard a loud scream! He was scared and started to run away.

But then he saw a strange symbol on the ground. He was curious and decided to take a closer look. He touched the symbol and all of a sudden he heard the scream again, but it was quieter this time. He was brave and stepped closer. The symbol glowed and a big bird flew out! 

Billy was amazed. He wanted to help the bird but then a loud, deep voice sounded. "The bird is mine," it said. It was the ancient guardian of the forest!

Billy was scared and ran away. The guardian screamed harder and followed him, but they couldn't catch Billy. Eventually, the guardian gave up and Billy was safe. He was happy he saved the bird and promised to never go back to the ancient forest again.

Once upon a time, a parrot lived in a big tree. The parrot was very proud of his pretty feathers. He liked to talk and dance all day long. The parrot had many friends in the forest.

One day, the parrot felt tired. He wanted to relax. So, he sat on a branch and closed his eyes. He did not see the big cat coming near the tree. The cat saw the parrot and wanted to catch him.

The cat climbed the tree very fast. The parrot did not hear the cat. The cat got closer and closer. The parrot was still relaxing with his eyes closed. Then, the cat jumped and caught the parrot. The proud parrot was not careful and now he was gone.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks and cars. One day, they find a big box of blocks in the playroom. They are happy and start to build a network of roads and bridges.

"Look, Mia, I made a long road!" Tom says.

"Wow, Tom, that's good! I made a high bridge!" Mia says.

They play for a while, but then Tom wants to make his road longer. He sees a block that Mia is using for her bridge. He takes it and puts it on his road.

"Hey, Tom, that's my block! Give it back!" Mia says.

"No, Mia, I need it for my road! It's mine now!" Tom says.

Mia is angry. She wants her block back. She tries to pull it from Tom's road, but Tom holds it tight. They start to tug and shout.

"Let go, Mia! It's mine!"

"Let go, Tom! It's mine!"

They tug harder and harder, until the block flies out of their hands. It hits the wall and breaks in two. They both gasp and stop.

"Oh no, the block is broken!" Tom says.

"Oh no, the bridge is ruined!" Mia says.

They look at each other and feel sad. They both like the block and the network. They don't like to fight and break things.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I shouldn't have taken your block," Mia says.

"I'm sorry, Mia. I shouldn't have pulled your block," Tom says.

They hug and say sorry. They decide to share the blocks and fix the network. They are friends again. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved to ride. Every day she would find something to ride on. 

One day she found a twig. It was a little twig. The girl was so excited that she could ride on it. 

She got on the twig and rode around the garden. She went faster and faster. She was having so much fun. 

The girl rode and rode until the sun went down. Then it was time for her to go home. 

But she was happy. She had had a great time riding on her little twig. She knew that she would have many more days of riding fun.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a fearful little girl named Lily. She was scared of many things, like loud noises and big dogs. One day, Lily was playing with her ball in the park when something strange happened.

A big motion came from the bushes. The leaves shook, and Lily felt scared. She held her ball tight and looked around. She wondered what could make such a big motion.

Then, out of the bushes came a little kitten. It was not scary at all! Lily felt happy and not fearful anymore. She played with the kitten and they became best friends. From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes things that seem scary at first can turn out to be nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a fragile doll that she loved very much. One night, she had a dream that her doll came to life and they went on an adventure together.

The next day, Lily was playing with her doll when her little brother came in and accidentally kicked the doll. Lily was very upset and started to cry. Her brother said, "I'm sorry, I didn't mean to kick your doll."

Lily wiped away her tears and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. But please be careful next time." Her brother nodded and promised to be more careful. From then on, Lily made sure to keep her fragile doll safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny things like rocks and shells. One day, she found a beautiful black crystal in the park. She was so happy and showed it to her mom.

Lily wanted to keep the crystal safe, so she put it in a special box. But the box was too high for her to reach. She tried and tried but couldn't succeed. Her mom saw her struggling and helped her get the box down.

Lily was so grateful and hugged her mom tightly. She succeeded in keeping her crystal safe and sound. From that day on, Lily kept her crystal in a special place where she could see it every day.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little bird that lived in the forest. One day, the bird was looking for food and found some seeds on the ground. It was very happy, and started to peck at the seeds. Suddenly, a rod crashed through the branches above, scattering the seeds everywhere. The little bird was scared and flew away, but soon realized it was just an old man.

The little bird waited until the old man was gone before coming back to the ground. There were still some scattered seeds left, and the little bird was very happy to get the last of them. The little bird was lucky that day, and the old man never knew he had scared it away!

Once there was a seal who lived far away in the sea. He was very happy but he was also very careless. He didnâ€™t pay enough attention to his surroundings and one day, he got too close to shore.

Once upon a time there was a man called Tim. He was very weak and always felt sad. One day, he was out trying to find some food when he suddenly saw something shiny. It was a knife! He was so excited, he picked it up and took it home.

At home, Tim examined the knife and found that it was very sharp and shiny. He knew that he could use it to cut food. He felt even more excited. 

He took the knife outside and tried to cut some vegetables. The vegetables were very hard and he had to push the knife very hard to cut them. He was so weak that he was having trouble.

Suddenly, the knife slipped and Tim caught his finger! He was very scared and started to cry. He ran home and his mom put a bandaid on it. She hugged him and told him that he had to be very careful next time. 

Tim was sad but he was still excited about his new knife. He made sure to be very careful from now on and it made him feel a lot better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her ball on the pitch near her house. One day, she saw a man walking by and asked him if he wanted to play too. The man said yes, but he looked anxious.

Lily and the man played together for a while, passing the ball back and forth. But then, the man suddenly kicked the ball too hard and it went over the fence. Lily was sad because she loved that ball very much.

The man apologized and promised to buy her a new ball. Lily forgave him and they continued to play together. The moral of the story is that sometimes accidents happen, but it's important to take responsibility for our actions and make things right.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to hide. One day, she wanted to find a new place to hide. She looked around her house and found an unknown place. 
It was a corner of her kitchen filled with jam. Everywhere she looked there was jam! She giggled and moved some of the jars aside. She crawled in and hid behind the jam jars.

Lucy started to sing her favorite song as she looked around. Nothing in the corner was familiar. She found something that looked like a button in the corner. She touched it and a panel opened up!

Inside, there was even more jam! Lucy couldn't believe how much jam she found. There were also some toys she had never seen before. She was so excited! She kept playing and having fun until her mom called her for dinner. 

When Lucy was finished eating, she went back to the corner and began to hide again. She played for hours, until finally it was time to go to bed. As she said goodnight and hugged her mom, she secretly smiled as she thought of her unknown hiding spot filled with jam.

Once upon a time, there was a big dinosaur who wanted to find a friend. He looked around everywhere but couldn't find anyone. He was beginning to feel sad and embarrassed so he decided to ask a wise old tree for help.

The tree thought for a while and then said, â€œI recommend that you look in the jungle. Youâ€™ll find lots of other animals there and you might be able to find a new friend.â€

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to play baseball. He played with his friends every day and they had so much fun. One day, the boy's mom asked him to take a nap because he looked very tired. The boy didn't want to nap, but he knew it was good for him.

While the boy was napping, his friends played baseball without him. They had a lot of fun, but they were also thoughtful and missed their friend. When the boy woke up from his nap, he was sad to see that his friends had played without him.

The boy felt left out and didn't want to play with his friends anymore. He stopped going outside and playing baseball altogether. His friends tried to talk to him, but he didn't want to listen. Eventually, the boy became very lonely and unhappy. He realized that taking a nap was important, but so was playing with his friends. Sadly, it was too late and he lost his friends forever. The end.

Sam was a happy little three-year-old child. He was always fascinated by the huge green port that was near his house. Every day he would go there and watch the boats come and go. 

One day, Sam noticed something was different. A big barge had come and dropped something off. It was a strange, new green boat. Sam decided to take a closer look. 

When Sam got closer, he saw a sailor who told him that the barge had brought the new green boat to replace the old one. Sam was so excited. He asked the sailor if he could help replace the boat. The sailor smiled and said, â€œSure, if itâ€™s OK with your mom.â€ 

Sam ran back home to ask his mom if he could help the sailor. After getting permission, Sam ran back to the port and with the help of the sailor, he helped to replace the old boat with the new one. 

Sam was so happy with his new accomplishment. He had never helped to replace a boat before and was proud of himself for doing it. From that day forward, Sam held a special place in his heart for the green port.

Once upon a time, there was a polite boy named Tim. He liked to play with his toys. One day, Tim found a toy weapon in his room. It was a sword. Tim was very happy.

Tim played with his new weapon all day. He pretended to be a brave knight. He fought dragons and monsters. But then, he heard a scream from outside.

Tim ran outside to see what was wrong. He saw a little girl who was scared of a big bug. Tim used his toy weapon to scare the bug away. The girl said "thank you" and they became friends. They played together with the toy sword and had a great day.

Once upon a time there was a large lion. He was very big and strong. He liked to roam around in the jungle.

One day, while in the jungle, he heard a little voice. He looked around but he couldn't see anything. Then he heard the voice again, only this time it was louder. The lion looked around and saw a small rabbit.

The rabbit said to the lion, "Hello. Do you understand me?". The lion shook his head, he didn't understand.

The rabbit said again, this time a bit slower. "Do you understand me?". The lion shook his head again. So the rabbit tried one more time, this time talking much slower and simpler.

Finally the lion nodded his head. He understood the rabbit. He smiled and said, "Yes, I do understand you". The rabbit was so happy. They became good friends.

Tom and Sue were brother and sister. They liked to play in the house, but they also liked to go outside. One day, they saw a big box in the yard. They wanted to see what was inside.

They tried to open the box, but it was locked. They looked for a key, but they could not find one. They asked their mom, but she said no. She said the box was not for them. She said it was for dad. She said he would be mad if they touched it.

Tom and Sue did not listen. They wanted to see what was inside. They waited until mom was busy. Then they sneaked out to the yard. They found a tool in the shed. They used it to unlock the box. They opened the lid and looked inside.

They saw a lot of dishes. They were shiny and pretty. They had flowers and birds on them. They were dad's gift for mom. He wanted to surprise her. He wanted to make her happy.

Tom and Sue did not know that. They thought the dishes were toys. They took them out of the box. They played with them. They threw them in the air. They smashed them on the ground. They made a lot of noise and a lot of mess.

Mom heard the noise. She came out to the yard. She saw the broken dishes. She saw Tom and Sue. She was very sad and very angry. She scolded them. She said they were naughty and selfish. She said they ruined dad's gift for mom. She said they had to say sorry and help clean up.

Tom and Sue felt bad. They realized they did a bad thing. They said sorry to mom. They said sorry to dad. They helped clean up. They learned a lesson. They learned to respect other people's things. They learned to listen to their mom. They learned to be good and kind.

Once upon a time, there was a big yellow flower called a sunflower. It was as tall as a house and had lots of seeds inside. One day, a little girl named Lily was playing in the garden and she saw the sunflower. She thought it was so pretty that she wanted to take a picture of it. She asked her mommy for her phone so she could record the sunflower.

But Lily was very careless and she dropped the phone on the ground. The phone broke and her mommy was very upset. Lily felt bad and promised to be more careful next time. She still loved the sunflower though, and she would always remember how pretty it was.

Once upon a time, there was a messy dog named Mark. Mark loved to play in the mud. One sunny day, Mark went to the park to play with his ball.

Mark saw a big goal on the grass. He wanted to kick the ball into the goal. He ran fast and kicked the ball with all his might. The ball flew into the goal. Mark was very happy.

Mark played all day until he was very tired. He went home to his bed, still messy from the mud. Mark's mom saw how messy he was and gave him a bath. Mark was clean and cozy in his bed, dreaming about his fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, in a lush and beautiful forest, lived a persistent deer. She was determined to find the perfect spot to eat some tasty grass and take a nap in the warm sun. Everywhere she looked seemed perfect - but she couldn't seem to settle on a spot. 

Suddenly, she heard laughter. Startled, the deer looked around and spotted a small girl playing in a nearby clearing. The girl's eyes lit up with glee as she spotted the deer and shouted: "Can I hold you?" The deer, feeling shy, shook her head and stepped back. 

The little girl was disappointed and kept insisting: "C'mon, please? I just want to hold you for a second!" The deer felt confused, but eventually agreed. The girl took a few steps forward, her arms outstretched, and reached for the deer. 

The deer jumped away quickly. She felt scared and wasn't sure what the girl wanted. The girl kept trying to reach for the deer but the deer didn't budge. In the end, the girl gave up and thanked the deer for playing with her. Then, after a few moments, the persistent deer continued her search for the perfect spot to take a nap in the sun.

Teddy was very eager to go outside and explore. His mom opened the front door and Teddy peeked out. He saw a shiny new bike and he started to jump around in excitement. He ran over to the bike and started to peddle. Teddy peddled around the front yard and he was so proud of himself. He kept peddling and he explored all around the neighborhood, showing off his new bike. He was so excited to explore. Eventually, it was time for Teddy to go in for the night. His mom smiled at his eagerness and Teddy couldn't wait to ride his bike again the following day.

Little Charlie and his Mum were walking in the park. Charlie saw a duck sitting in a row by the pond. The duck looked fit, so Charlie wanted to save it.

Mum said that Charlie couldn't, but she could help. She went and got a net from the pond keeper and carefully crept up to the duck and put the net over it.

The duck was upset and quacked loudly. But Charlie was brave and he held the net so the duck couldn't get away. Mum then put the duck in a bag, and Charlie grinned.

They took the duck to a special duck pond away from the park. When they released it, the duck immediately flew away to its friends.

Mum said, "Well done Charlie, you saved the duck." Charlie smiled proudly and said, "I'm a fit duck saver!"

Once there was a little girl. She was very happy, but she was also very pale.

One day she decided to go on an adventure. She put on her hat and left the house.

She walked for a while and then she saw something. It was a tree with a big green yogurt on top of it! She jumped up to get it but it was too high. 

She started to cry, but then another person came and gave her the yogurt. She was so happy and thanked the person.

She took a big bite out of the yogurt and then she said goodbye and left. 

She was never so happy to be on an adventure before. She walked home with a big smile on her face and a pale yogurt in her hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy navy ships in the bathtub. One day, his mom told him it was time to get out of the tub and go to bed. 

Timmy promised his mom that he would be obedient and go to bed right away. But instead of going to bed, he snuck back into the bathroom to play with his navy ships some more. 

Suddenly, Timmy knocked over the bottle of bubble bath and made a big mess. His mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She was very upset and told Timmy that he had broken his promise to be obedient. 

Timmy was sad and went to bed feeling guilty. The next day, he apologized to his mom and promised to be more obedient in the future. From then on, Timmy always kept his promises and was a good boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but his room was always messy. His mom told him to clean up his toys, but he didn't want to. 

One day, Timmy's mom said she would send his toys to the toy donation center if he didn't clean up his room. Timmy didn't want to lose his toys, so he started to clean up. He put his toys away in an organized way, so he could find them later. 

As he was cleaning, Timmy accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke on the floor. He was sad, but he knew he had to clean it up. He got a broom and swept up the pieces. His mom was proud of him for being responsible and cleaning up the mess. From that day on, Timmy always kept his room organized and clean.

Once upon a time, there were two twins. They looked the same and liked to play together. One day, their mommy told them to dress up for a party. The twins were excited and went to their room to find their humble clothes. They put on their best dresses and looked very pretty. At the party, everyone said they looked lovely and the twins were very happy. They danced and played and had a lot of fun together. The end.

Mum and Dad were sewing some clothes. They had some purple thread that they were using to make a dress, but it wasn't going as planned. 

Mum asked, "What's wrong Dad?"

Dad frowned, then said, "This thread is terrible. It's so hard to sew with."

Mum smiled and took the thread. She easily threaded it through the needle, showing Dad how it was done. 

"You have to be gentle," she said. 

Dad tried again, with Mum's help, and it worked! He looked surprised, but then he smiled.

"Why don't you practice with some easier threads," Mum said.

Dad started to practice and soon he was able to thread even the thickest and most difficult of threads. They finished the dress and it looked amazing! 

Mum and Dad smiled and hugged, happy that Dad got the hang of sewing with thread.

Once upon a time, a little duck named Ducky wanted to swim in the pond. But when she got there, she saw a big frog sitting on a lily pad. The frog said, "This is my pond. You can't swim here."

Ducky was sad. She really wanted to swim in the pond. She decided to go on an adventure to discover a new pond. She walked and walked until she found a unique pond with no frogs in it. She was so happy and she swam all day long.

But when she got back to her pond, the frog was still there. Ducky told the frog about her adventure and how she found a new pond. The frog was impressed and said, "I guess you can swim in this pond too." Ducky was happy to have a new friend and a new pond to swim in.

Once upon a time, there was a baby elephant named Shadow. Shadow was very clumsy. One day, Shadow was playing in the grass when he fell down and broke his bone. Shadow felt so sad and he tried to get up but with only one bone, it was too difficult.

Shadow's mother came over to help him out. She said, "Don't worry Shadow, I will get you a new bone!" She carefully lifted him up and took him to the animal doctor.

The animal doctor looked at Shadow and said, "Hmmm, I have something that can help you!" He reached into a draw and pulled out a big, thick bone. He said, "Let me replace this tough bone for the one that broke and Shadow will be as good as new!"

Shadow smiled and thanked the doctor. His mother couldn't believe how quickly the doctor replaced Shadow's broken bone. Shadow was so happy and hopped away with his new bone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Mikey who really liked to watch cartoons. One day, he was watching his favourite cartoon when he heard a noise outside. He got up to take a look, but all he could see was a big nosy dog. "Woof!" said the dog.

Mikey got scared and shouted, "Go away, dog!" But the dog didn't move. Mikey was so mad. He picked up a big stick and tried to scare the dog off, but it was no use. The dog just kept on barking.

Then, out of nowhere, Mikey heard a voice behind him. It was coming from inside his house. "No need to be so nosy, silly dog," said the voice. Mikey turned around and saw his mom, who was shaking her head at the dog and smiling. Mikey laughed and said to the dog, "You better listen to my mom!"

The dog finally left and Mikey went back to watching his cartoon. He had learned to be brave, even though sometimes he forgot to listen. From then on, he knew that his mom would always set him right.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Alex. She was very brave and strong.

Alex liked to explore, so one day she decided to take a walk outside. Everywhere she looked, she knew she was safe. She felt very brave and strong.

As she kept walking, she saw something. It was a big, furry animal with a long, bushy tail. Alex thought it was so cool, but she didn't know what it was. 

The furry animal was really friendly and Alex decided to pet it. She was amazed at how soft and cuddly it was! As the animal followed her around, Alex knew she was safe. 

The furry animal stayed with Alex for the whole day. She was so happy that she found a new friend that she could feel safe and strong with. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, they decided to measure how tall they were. Lily was the shortest of all her friends, but that didn't make her sad.

As they were playing, Lily stumbled and fell down. Her friends rushed to help her and asked if she was okay. Lily said she was fine and got up with a smile on her face. They continued playing, but Lily thought the game was boring. She wanted to do something else.

So, Lily suggested they play hide-and-seek instead. Her friends agreed and they had a lot of fun. Lily stumbled a few more times while running, but she didn't mind. She was happy to be playing with her friends and having a good time.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Thomas. He was three years old.

One day, Thomas took his cooler to the beach. It was full of sweet treats. Suddenly, the phone in Thomas's pocket began to ring.

Thomas answered the call and began to talk to his mom. "Mom! I'm at the beach with my cooler! It's so cool!"

"That sounds fun," said his mom. "Make sure to stay cool while you're there. Don't forget to put your cooler in the shade too!"

Thomas thanked his mom and hung up. He grabbed his cooler and found a shady spot to put it down. The sun was hot, but his cooler was nice and cool.

As Thomas enjoyed the sweet treats from his cooler, he forgot all about the phone call!

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. But sometimes they disagreed about what to play.

One day, Ben wanted to play pirates. He had a hat, a sword and a map. He said, "Arrr, matey, let's find the treasure in the world!"

But Lily wanted to play fairies. She had a dress, a wand and a crown. She said, "No, thank you, let's fly to the magic kingdom!"

They both looked at each other. They were confused. Why did they want to play different things? They did not like to disagree. They wanted to have fun.

Then they had an idea. They decided to play pirates and fairies together. Ben said, "OK, you can be a fairy pirate. You can use your wand to help us find the treasure."

Lily said, "OK, you can be a pirate fairy. You can use your sword to protect us from the bad guys."

They smiled and hugged. They were happy. They agreed to play pirates and fairies in the world. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a red cap that he wore every day. He loved his cap very much.

One day, Tim could not find his cap. He was worried. He looked under his bed, in his toy box, and even in the kitchen. But his cap was not there. Tim asked his mom, "Mom, have you seen my red cap?"

His mom said, "Yes, I have. It was dirty, so I washed it. It's hanging outside to dry." Tim went outside and saw his cap hanging on the line. He was so happy. He waited for his cap to dry, and then he put it back on his head.

From that day on, Tim always knew where his cap was. He never felt worried about his cap again. And every time his cap got dirty, he would ask his mom to wash it for him. They lived happily ever after.

One day, a little cat went out to search for a toy. The cat looked and looked, but could not find it. The cat felt sad because the toy was its favorite. It was a long, soft toy that the cat loved to hug.

As the cat walked, it saw a big stand with many toys on it. The cat thought, "Maybe my toy is there!" The cat looked at the stand, but the toy was not there. The cat felt even more sad.

Just then, a nice dog came by. The dog saw the sad cat and asked, "Why are you sad?" The cat told the dog about the long toy. The dog said, "I will help you search!" They looked and looked, and finally found the toy under a big tree. The cat was so happy and thanked the dog. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie loved to play in the jungle with her friends. One day, Ellie and her friends were playing a game of hide-and-seek. Ellie found the perfect hiding spot behind a big tree. 

Suddenly, Ellie heard a loud noise. She peeked out from behind the tree and saw a mischievous monkey with a can of spray paint. The monkey was marking the trees with bright colors. Ellie knew this was not allowed in the jungle. 

Ellie quietly snuck up behind the monkey and sprayed him with water from her trunk. The monkey was surprised and ran away. Ellie saved the trees from being marked with paint and her friends were very proud of her. From that day on, Ellie was known as the protector of the jungle.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was walking in a park one day and suddenly the sun disappeared. Everything got dark and Lucy got nervous. She didn't know what to do.

Lucy felt much better after the owl had spoken to her. She knew the sun would be back soon and that she had a friend to watch over her.

The sun reappeared and Lucy waved goodbye to the owl as she continued to explore the park. She will never forget the owl that made her feel safe when the sun had disappeared.

Once upon a time there was a little bear. He lived in a small house in the woods. He was lonely and wished he had a friend.

Once upon a time there was a black radish. He was very happy in his radish patch, but one day something strange happened.

The black radish was shaking and he felt very scared. Then, he heard a voice. "What are you shaking for?" it said. 

The black radish looked up and saw a friendly looking rabbit. He said, "I'm shaking because I'm scared. I don't know why I'm shaking!"

The rabbit smiled and said, "Don't worry. I'll help you feel better. I'm going to give you a big hug. That'll make you feel much better."

Once upon a time there was a small lion named Felix. He was very brave and could scare anyone who made him angry. Every day, he would walk into the wilderness in search of adventure.

One day, Felix came across a tiny inchworm on the side of the path.

The worm looked very sad and Felix wanted to help it. He asked the worm why it was so sad, but it just shrugged its shoulders.

Felix tried to make the worm feel better by talking to it and offering it small treats. Nothing seemed to work and the small worm kept shrugging.

Finally, Felix decided to pick up the inchworm and carry it into the nearby forest. He would carry it all the way home, where it could be safe and happy.

Unfortunately, the journey was too much for the inchworm. By the time Felix made it home, the inchworm had died. Felix was heartbroken and he felt so sad.

The end.

Tommy likes to play with his rubber ball. He can bounce it, throw it, and catch it. He has fun with his ball every day.

One day, Tommy wants to try something new. He sees a big hill near his house. He thinks it would be fun to roll his ball down the hill and see how far it goes. He runs to the hill with his ball.

He puts his ball on the top of the hill and gives it a push. The ball starts to roll down the hill very fast. Tommy runs after it, but he cannot catch it. The ball goes faster and faster, and Tommy gets tired.

The ball reaches the bottom of the hill and keeps rolling. It rolls into a pond. The pond is cold and deep. Tommy stops at the edge of the pond and looks at his ball. He is sad. He cannot get his ball back.

Then he sees a duck. The duck is swimming in the pond. The duck sees the ball and swims to it. The duck picks up the ball with its beak and brings it to Tommy. Tommy is happy. He thanks the duck and takes his ball. He hugs his ball and smiles.

Tommy learned something new. He learned that rolling his ball down the hill is not a good idea. He also learned that ducks are nice and can help. He decides to play with his ball in his yard instead. He succeeds in having fun with his ball and making a new friend.

One day, a gentle penguin was released into the sea. He was so excited to explore and see what he could find. He thought he saw a shiny fish and paddled close. When the penguin was close, the shiny fish asked, "Do you want to come with me?" The penguin thought this sounded like a fun adventure and said yes right away.

Before he knew it, the sweet penguin was taken far away, and he was scared to be so far from home. He tried to paddle away but the fish was too strong. The fish started to laugh and said, "You can't escape, I'm keeping you here!" He soon realized this was not an adventure, but a trap.

The gentle penguin was unable to escape and stayed in the trap forever. He missed his home and wished he had not been so eager for an adventure. The poor penguin had a bad ending, and he never saw his home again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to visit her grandma's house. One day, Lily's mom asked her to bring some juice for her grandma. Lily was nervous because she had never gone alone before. 

Lily took the juice and started walking to her grandma's house. She saw a stray dog on the way and got scared. But she remembered her mom's words, "Don't be nervous, just be brave." So, she walked past the dog and reached her grandma's house safely. 

Her grandma was very happy to see her and praised her for being so brave. Lily felt proud of herself and learned that being brave is important. From that day on, she was never nervous to visit her grandma's house alone.

Mary was a very adventurous girl. She loved going on adventures and exploring the world. One day, Mary was walking around in the forest when she spotted a magical talking fork! Mary was so excited! She ran over and picked up the fork.
