The next day, Mary said goodbye to her new friends and thanked the fork for showing her this amazing adventure. She hugged the fork and waved goodbye as she headed home. From that day on, Mary was always adventurous and ready for her next amazing adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bunny. One day, the bunny wanted to take a shower. So, the bunny went into the shower and turned on the water. The bunny loved the warm water and stayed in the shower for a long time.

After the bunny finished taking a shower, it went to play outside. But, the bunny didn't see the big, scary dog that was nearby. The dog started chasing the bunny and the bunny tried to run away. But, the bunny couldn't run fast enough and the dog caught it.

The bunny couldn't stay safe from the dog and got hurt. The bunny's friends were sad and cried for the cute bunny. The end.

Once upon a time in the wild forest, there was a little girl. She had an axe, and she loved to number the trees. She would count them one by one as she walked.

Every day, she found a new and exciting thing in the forest. She saw wild animals and furry bunnies, and she even saw a big bear! One day, she found an old tree with a huge axe stuck in it.

The little girl tried to pull the axe out, but it was too heavy! She kept trying and trying and eventually, the axe was free. She was so excited! She thought it was really cool!

The little girl took the axe home with her, and she was so happy to show it to her family. She had found a real, wild axe in the forest! She couldn't believe it, and neither could her family.

From that day on, the little girl and her axe were inseparable! She went on all sorts of adventures together, numbering trees, finding wild animals and exploring the secrets of the forest.

Jimmy was a curious three-year-old. One day he got out of bed and went to his mom in the kitchen. She smiled and asked him what he wanted.

"I want to know what's outside," Jimmy said.

His mom explained that outside was the world around him. There was the garden on one side and the driveway on the other. The garden had lots of open spaces with flowers and trees. The driveway was wide and open and it led to a road.

Jimmy was amazed. He couldn't wait to explore the outside world. His mom told him he could go, but he had to be careful. Jimmy smiled excitedly, thanked his mom and ran outside. He opened the door and was greeted by a bright, new world full of possibilities.

Once upon a time, there was a king who had a powerful crown. He loved his crown very much and wore it every day. One day, a bad man came and stole the crown from the king. The king was very sad and cried a lot.

The bad man wore the crown and felt very powerful. He gained control over the kingdom and made the people do bad things. The king tried to get his crown back but the bad man was too strong. 

In the end, the bad man became very greedy and wanted more power. He started to fight with other kingdoms and lost his own kingdom. The crown was lost forever and the king never got it back. The kingdom was never the same again.

Once there was a little girl named May. May was a curious person who liked to explore. She found an old mill and wanted to see what was inside.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Timmy and Tommy. They loved to play together every day. One day, they went outside to play in the rain. They jumped in puddles and got very wet.

Suddenly, Timmy saw a big stick and wanted to play with it. But Tommy also wanted to play with it. They started to quarrel and argue about who could play with the stick. They both wanted it very much.

Their argument got very tight and they both started to cry. Then, Timmy had an idea. He said, "Let's share the stick. You can play with it first, then I can play with it later." Tommy thought that was a great idea and they both smiled. They played with the stick together and their friendship became even stronger.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Josh. He was three years old. Josh wanted a goat very much. He asked his mom could he get a goat, but she said no.

Once upon a time, there was a daisy. It was a very thin daisy. The daisy was sad because it was so thin. One day, it started to rain. The rain was very soft, and soon it was over. The daisy was happy! Its thin stem started to grow and soon it was very strong. Every day it grew a bit bigger, until it was a tall daisy with lots of happy petals. All of the petals were very bright and colourful. The daisy was so happy. Everyone said it was the happiest daisy that ever grew!

The little girl was fearful. She hid behind some furniture and was scared to peek out. Suddenly, she heard strange noises from the kitchen. She slowly peeped out from behind the furniture and saw an old man stirring something in a pot. 

She wanted to call for help, but she was too scared. She tried to keep quiet even as the old man's stirring got louder and louder. Then, the old man stopped. He smiled at the little girl and said, "What's your name, my dear?"
 
The little girl was so relieved. She went to the old man and said her name. Then, the old man asked her if she wanted a bowl of soup. He said it would make her feel better. The little girl said yes, and the old man stirred the soup while she watched. 

Soon enough, the little girl's fear faded away. After eating her soup, she thanked the old man and happily went home.

Once upon a time, there was a sister who was very elderly. Every morning, she would bow to the sun, to show her respect. 

Her little sister, who was only three years old, wanted to join her. 

"Will you teach me how to bow too?" She asked.

The elder sister smiled. "Of course, little one. Follow me and I will show you how it's done."

She bowed deeply, and the little one did her best to copy. But when the sun shined brightly, she was too shy to bow as far as her elder sister did. 

The elder sister frowned, and said, "I want to show the sun my respect, but you are not bowing deeply enough. Will you try again and show the sun your respect?" 

The little one nodded, and the next morning the sun shined even brighter. Taking a deep breath, she bravely bowed twice as deeply as before to show her respect. 

Her elder sister smiled, proud of her little sister for showing the sun respect. The sun smiled too, for it did not need much to be respected, only a willing heart.

Once upon a time, there was a large bear named Bobo. Bobo loved to wear a big red tube around his neck. He thought it made him look very cool.

One day, Bobo went for a walk in the forest. He saw a little bird who was stuck in a tree. The bird asked Bobo for help. Bobo used his large red tube to help the bird. He put the tube around the tree and pulled it down. The bird was free!

The little bird was so happy that Bobo helped. They became best friends. Bobo and the bird would play together every day. And Bobo always wore his big red tube, because it reminded him of the day he met his best friend.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play and eat. One day, they see a big jar of butter in the kitchen. They love butter on their bread.

"Let's take some butter," Tim says. "Mom won't know."

"OK," Kim says. "But how do we get it?"

Tim has a creative idea. He gets a chair and a spoon. He climbs on the chair and reaches for the jar. He scoops some butter with the spoon and puts it in his pocket.

"Good job, Tim," Kim says. "Now it's my turn."

She gets another spoon and climbs on the chair. She also scoops some butter and puts it in her pocket.

They are very happy. They run to their room with their butter. They find some bread and make butter sandwiches. They eat and smile.

But they don't know that Mom is watching. She sees them steal the butter. She is not happy. She goes to their room and knocks on the door.

"Tim and Kim, what are you doing?" she asks.

They look at Mom. They see her angry face. They feel bad.

"We are sorry, Mom," they say. "We took some butter. We were hungry."

Mom sighs. She knows they like butter. But she also knows they should not steal.

"Tim and Kim, stealing is wrong," she says. "You should ask me first. And you should not put butter in your pocket. It will make a mess."

She shows them their pockets. They are full of melted butter. It drips on the floor.

They see their pockets. They are shocked. They did not think of that.

"Oops," they say.

Mom shakes her head. She makes them clean their pockets and the floor. She also makes them share the rest of the butter with their brother and sister.

They learn their lesson. They do not steal butter again. They ask Mom first. And they use a plate.

Once there was a girl named Joe who was very impatient. She wanted to win a game.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who wanted more friends. So the fish decided to come and explore the big wide ocean. On the way, the fish found the sea was filled with so many strange new creatures.

Eventually the fish had to return home, but the sea turtle promised that the fish would always be welcome if ever he wanted to come back. And the fish found himself surrounded by many new friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alice. Alice was walking along the beach one day when suddenly she spotted a crab. The crab had a big frown on its face. Alice wanted to help and so she reached out her hand to pat the crab. But before she could, the crab scuttled away.

The birds were very sad. They had to spend all day collecting the seeds and fixing the glass. In the end, their mommy was still very angry and she flew away.

The birds were all alone with no one to comfort them. They had learned their lesson, but it was a very bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a big yard with a purple swing. She loved to play outside and swing high in the sky.

One sunny day, Amy went to the yard with her friend, Max. Max saw the purple swing and said, "Wow! I want to swing too!" Amy smiled and said, "Okay, let's swing together!"

They took turns on the purple swing, laughing and having fun. They swung so high, they felt like they could touch the sky. After a while, they got tired and sat down on the soft grass. They looked at each other, happy to have spent the day swinging in the yard.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a cozy house with her mommy and daddy. One day, she saw a bird fly into the chimney. She wanted to help the bird, so she asked her mommy and daddy to help her.

"I saw a bird fly into the chimney. Can we help it?" asked Lily.

Her mommy and daddy discussed it and decided to call a chimney sweep to help. The chimney sweep came and took the bird out of the chimney. Lily was happy that the bird was safe.

Later that day, Lily's mommy and daddy praised her for being honest and telling them about the bird. They told her that it's always important to tell the truth. Lily felt proud of herself for doing the right thing. From that day on, she always looked out for animals in need.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a little sword that he loved to play with. He would swing it around and pretend to be a brave knight.

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his sword. But then, he saw a big dog that made him worry. The dog barked loudly and Timmy felt scared. He didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a bigger boy came and scared the dog away. Timmy was happy that he was safe, but he felt sad that he couldn't protect himself. From that day on, Timmy decided to practice with his little sword every day so that he could be brave like the bigger boy.

One night, Ben and Lily were in their room. They wanted to play, but it was dark. Mom and Dad said they had to sleep. Ben had an idea. He took his flashlight from under his bed. He whispered to Lily, "Let's make shadows on the wall."

Lily nodded. She liked shadows. They were fun and funny. Ben turned on the flashlight and pointed it at the wall. He made his hand look like a rabbit. Lily giggled. She made her hand look like a bird. They made the rabbit and the bird talk to each other.

"Hello, Mr. Rabbit. How are you?" Lily said in a high voice.

"Hello, Miss Bird. I am fine. Do you want to play?" Ben said in a low voice.

"Yes, please. What do you want to play?" Lily said.

Suddenly, the door opened. It was Mom. She looked serious. She said, "What are you two doing? It's past your bedtime. Turn off the flashlight and go to sleep."

Ben and Lily felt scared. They did not want to make Mom angry. Ben turned off the flashlight and put it back under his bed. He said, "Sorry, Mom. We were just playing."

Mom sighed. She said, "I know, but you need to sleep. It's good for you. I love you, but you have to follow the rules." She tucked them in and kissed them goodnight. She said, "Sweet dreams, my little ones."

Ben and Lily said, "Goodnight, Mom. We love you too." They closed their eyes and tried to sleep. But they still thought about the shadows. They smiled and whispered, "That was fun."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who wanted to marry a prince. She looked all around her kingdom, but she couldn't find the right prince. One day, she saw a handsome prince in the traffic. She knew he was the one she wanted to marry.

The princess went to the prince and asked him to marry her. He said yes, and they had a big wedding. The wedding was so tight that everyone had to squeeze together to fit in the castle. But it was a happy day for everyone, and the princess and prince lived happily ever after.

One day, a girl named Jane went for a walk in the park. She felt so sleepy that she yawned. She saw some pretty flowers and bright birds. It made her smile. Then she spotted something even better. It was a big plate of candy lying on the ground! Jane was so happy. She quickly grabbed the candy and ran over to a nearby bench. 

Jane shared the candy with a little boy. "Thank you," he said. Jane smiled. She said, "Would you like to play together?" The little boy nodded. They laughed and played in the park. 

As the sun started to set, Jane and the little boy said goodbye. Jane was so tired that she yawned. She was ready to go home. But before she left, Jane looked back and waved goodbye. The little boy waved back, smiling. It was a very pretty day.

Once upon a time, there was a light little bird named Blue. Blue loved to bathe in the sun every day. Blue would fly to the top of a tree and find a nice spot to sit. Blue would then spread its wings and let the sun shine on them.

One day, Blue saw a tiny inch worm on a leaf. The inch worm was green and wiggled its way along the leaf. Blue thought the inch worm was funny and wanted to play. So, Blue flew down from the tree and said "Hi" to the inch worm. The inch worm wiggled and said "Hi" back.

Blue and the inch worm became friends. They played together every day. Blue would fly around the inch worm, and the inch worm would wiggle and dance. They had so much fun in the sun. And every day, Blue would still bathe in the sun with its new friend, the inch worm, by its side.

Once there was a boy called Max. He was three years old and he liked to watch movies. One day he was at the park with his family. He was feeling fine and he ran around and chased the birds.

Suddenly, he felt his foot slip and he fell to the ground. He started to cry, but his dad came over and helped him get up. He was all right and his dad was happy too.

They all went to the movies that evening. Max liked the movie because it was fine. He didn't even think about falling. He just enjoyed the movie and all the fun with his family.

Anna likes to collect stamps. She has a big book with many stamps from different places. She is very intelligent and knows a lot about the stamps. She likes to show her book to her friends and tell them stories.

One day, Anna brings her book to school. She wants to share it with her teacher and her classmates. But when she puts her book on the table, a boy named Ben sees it. Ben is not very nice. He likes to take things from other kids and make them cry.

Ben waits until Anna is not looking. Then he sneaks to the table and grabs her book. He runs away with it and laughs. Anna sees him and gets very sad and angry. She shouts, "Ben, give me back my book! That is mine!"

Ben does not listen. He opens the book and looks at the stamps. He thinks they are boring. He decides to remove some of the stamps and stick them on his face. He thinks he looks funny and cool. He shows his face to the other kids and makes fun of Anna.

Anna runs after him and tries to get her book back. She says, "Ben, stop it! You are ruining my stamps! They are very special and important to me!" But Ben does not care. He keeps removing more stamps and sticking them on his face and his clothes. He thinks he is smarter than Anna.

But then, something bad happens. The stamps are very sticky and hard to take off. Ben tries to remove them from his face and his clothes, but they hurt him. He cries out, "Ow, ow, ow! It hurts! Help me!"

Anna hears him and feels sorry for him. She is still angry, but she is also kind. She goes to him and helps him remove the stamps. She says, "Ben, you should not have taken my book and my stamps. That was very mean and silly. You should say sorry and be nice to me and the other kids."

Ben feels ashamed and sorry. He says, "I'm sorry, Anna. I was wrong. I did not know the stamps were so sticky and hard to remove. I did not mean to hurt you or your stamps. You are very intelligent and your stamps are very interesting. Can you forgive me?"

Anna smiles and says, "Yes, I can forgive you, Ben. But you have to promise me to never do that again. And you have to help me fix my book and my stamps. They are very precious to me."

Ben nods and says, "I promise, Anna. And I will help you. Maybe you can teach me more about the stamps and the places they come from. I want to learn from you."

Anna and Ben hug and make up. They go back to the table and work on the book and the stamps together. They become friends and share their stories. The teacher and the other kids are happy to see them get along. They all learn something new and have fun.

John was a little boy who really loved cars. He had a big red car and it was his favourite. Every day, he would take his car for a drive.

One day, John was driving around when he drove into a dark tunnel. He could hardly see anything but he kept driving until suddenly, he heard a loud crash. His car had gone over a broken fence at the end of the tunnel.

John got out of his car and looked at the broken fence. He thought it was so strange. He wanted to know who had put the fence there. 

Just then, a big bus drove up to the tunnel. Out popped a friendly man who said to John, "What are you doing in this tunnel?" John told the man about the broken fence and asked him who had put it up.

The man smiled and said, "I'm the one who built this fence and put it here. You see, I wanted to keep everyone safe and make sure that no one got hurt by driving into this tunnel. But it looks like my fence is broken now."

John thanked the man for being so kind and said goodbye. He drove away happy and content, having cleared up the mystery of the broken fence in the tunnel.

Once upon a time there was a town that glowed at night. All the houses and shops had special lights that shone so brightly. Everyone in the town was so spoiled; they had all they needed. Everyone shared lots of things and there was kindness all around.

One night something extra special happened. The town was glowing even brighter than usual. Little Peter looked out his window and rubbed his eyes, for the town had become more magical than ever before.

Sparkles were shooting out from the town and everyone cheered. But then, something funny happened. A rainbow dragon came flying down from the sky. It was carrying a big bag of treats for everyone in the town. Soon the town was filled with laughter and joy from all the lucky people who got their treats.

All the people of the town had never been so spoiled! And from that day on, the town kept glowing brighter and brighter every night. That's why no matter how dark it gets the town of lights will always shine.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore and go on adventures. One day, he found a map that showed a treasure hidden in the forest. Timmy was eager to find the treasure, so he followed the map.

As he walked through the forest, he met a man who was selling apples. Timmy asked the man if he had seen the treasure, but the man had not. However, the man gave Timmy an apple to eat on his journey.

Timmy continued on his adventure and finally found the treasure. He was so happy and excited! He ran back to the man selling apples and showed him the treasure. The man was amazed and gave Timmy another apple as a reward.

From that day on, Timmy and the man became good friends and went on many adventures together, always eager to find new treasures.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Zoe. Zoe liked to explore, so one day she went to the park with her friends. At the park, Zoe spotted a beautiful palm tree. She thought it would be fun to steal one of its leaves. She gently touched the soft green leaf and slowly pulled it off. She was excited to show her friends!

Just then, a park guard came to investigate what was going on. Zoe was so surprised she dropped the leaf. The guard saw it and asked Zoe to give it back. Zoe quickly nodded her head and carefully returned the leaf back to the palm tree.

The guard thanked Zoe for her honesty and sent her and her friends off with a warning. Zoe was embarrassed but also happy to learn about the importance of not stealing. She promised to never do it again!

From then on, Zoe was very careful of what she touched at the park. Whenever she saw a beautiful leaf, she admired it from afar and appreciated its soft beauty.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Bella. Bella wanted to go fishing with her dad. 
Her dad thought it was a good idea and suggested she find a net. He said it didn't need to be a fancy one, just a simple one would be enough. 

Bella started looking around the house and soon found a net. But when she looked at it she noticed it had a hole. Her dad saw it too and looked very serious. He said they would have to buy a new net.

So they went to the store and found a big, new net. It was yellow and looked very serious. Bella felt so excited she almost started jumping. 

With their new net they headed to the lake. Dad showed Bella how to use it and soon they had caught a fish! It was a blooming success and dad was very proud of Bella.

There was a kangaroo that wanted to find a new home. He hopped around searching but he couldn't find the right place. Everywhere he looked the air was too cold.

He kept hopping until he found a warm, cozy cave. But when he went inside, he saw that someone else was already living there. It was a family of koalas! 

The kangaroo asked if he could stay. The koalas welcomed him and he was so happy. The kangaroo was so comfortable in the cave and he had plenty of food to eat. He finally had a home.

The kangaroo and the koalas all shared the cave and were happy to have a friend. They all enjoyed basking in the warm cave when the outside air was too cold.

Henry was in his bedroom, looking through his drawers. He wanted something special to do, but nothing seemed exciting. Then, he noticed a plain, ordinary drawer. He opened it and, to Henry's surprise, a tiny creature was inside! The creature, which had bright red eyes, said hello. Henry replied, "Oh, hello, who are you?" The creature told Henry that its name was Percy, and that it lived inside this ordinary drawer.

Henry thought this was very strange, but he decided to ask Percy what it wanted. Percy said it wanted company, as it was lonely living in the drawer all by itself. Henry immediately felt bad for Percy, and he asked how he could help. Percy replied that Henry could take it out for adventures, so Henry quickly agreed. 

However, Henry's parents said that it wasn't a good idea. They said Henry had to put Percy back in the drawer and leave it there, as it was too dangerous to take outside. Henry disagreed, and he said they should at least let Percy have some friends. After a short argument, Henry's parents said they would think about it. 

Henry was relieved and gave Percy a big smile. He knew that his parents were usually reasonable, so he was sure the two of them would come up with a solution soon. Little Percy was very excited too and, in that moment, it felt like nothing could stop them.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved playing with his dog, Max. Max was a big, brown dog with a mild temper. One day, Tim and Max were playing in the park when a loud noise disturbed them. 

Max barked loudly and Tim asked, "What's wrong, Max?" Max didn't answer, but continued to bark. Suddenly, a small bird flew out of a nearby tree and Max chased after it. 

Tim called out to Max, "Come back, Max! You're scaring the bird!" Max stopped and looked back at Tim. "Sorry," Max barked. "I didn't mean to disturb the bird." Tim smiled and patted Max's head. "It's okay, Max. Let's go home now." 

And so, Tim and Max went home, happy and tired from their day in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. She was the happiest three year old around. One day, Mary went to the park with her mom. She saw a net lying on the ground and wondered what it was for. She asked her mom and she said it was for catching butterflies. 

Mary was so excited! With her mom's help, she started weaving the net like a spiderweb. When she was done, they went out to the garden and waited for the butterflies to come.
 
Sure enough, a few beautiful, charming butterflies flew by and Mary finished her net. She gracefully placed it over the butterflies and, sure enough, she had caught them. She was so happy and excited that she ran around the garden in excitement. 

At the end of the day, Mary had caught some of the most beautiful and charming butterflies in the world. What a wonderful day she had!

Once upon a time, there was a patient dog named Lucky. He lived in a loving home and was always looked after by his family.

One day, Lucky was walking down a pathway in the forest when suddenly he stumbled upon a bear cub. Lucky barked and the cub ran away. When Lucky's family found out, they were so happy that he had been brave enough to protect them. 

Lucky's family rewarded him with a treat and said, "Lucky, you are such a patient and brave dog! We love you very much!"

Lucky was so excited to get the treat that he started jumping around the room. The family laughed and then ordered him to sit. 

Lucky was so excited and so lucky to have such a loving family.

Once, there was a man who was very crazy. He wanted to do something special with paint. So, he decided to raise it up the wall! He had many colors of paint and started raising it slowly, up and up and up the wall. He started to get creative with the colors and soon it was transformed into a beautiful painting. He was so proud of his work. Everyone around him was amazed at how crazy it looked. He completely transformed the wall with paint and everyone was happy.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient scooter. It had traveled all around the world, and it had so many stories to tell.

One day, the scooter was asked to deliver a special package. The package was so big and it took the scooter a very long time to deliver. But the scooter was brave and trundled along on its journey.

Finally, the scooter arrived at its destination. When it was time to deliver the package, the scooter was relieved! Everyone cheered in happiness and thanked the scooter for it's hard work. The scooter had done it, it had delivered the package!

The scooter was so proud and happy that it decided to celebrate by riding around the town. It whizzed through the streets and went so fast! People cheered as the ancient scooter rode by.

The scooter knew that it had achieved something special that day, something it would never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little dog named Toby. Toby loved to stir his water bowl with his paw. One day, Toby's family went on a holiday, and they took Toby with them.

On the holiday, Toby met a new friend named Daisy. Daisy was a small bird who liked to sing. Toby asked Daisy, "Do you like to stir things too?" Daisy said, "No, I like to sing. But I can try to stir with you!" They played together, and Toby showed Daisy how to stir.

As they stirred and played, they made a big mess. Toby's family saw the mess and said, "Toby, you need to learn to be careful when you play." Toby and Daisy felt sad, but they learned that it is important to be careful and not make a mess. From that day on, they played together carefully and had lots of fun on their holiday.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a calm dog who liked to sit on his stand and watch the birds fly by. One day, Spot saw a big tree and birds were singing in it. He decided to go near the tree and listen to the birds.

As Spot walked to the tree, he met a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers was sitting under the tree and looking up at the birds. Spot said, "Hi Whiskers, do you like the birds too?" Whiskers looked at him and said, "Yes, Spot. I love to watch them sing and play."

Spot and Whiskers decided to sit under the tree together and listen to the birds. They were both very calm and happy. The birds saw them and sang even louder. Spot and Whiskers became good friends and they always met under the tree to enjoy the birds' songs.

One day, a lively dog named Spot came to a new home. He was so happy to arrive at the big house. Spot wagged his tail and jumped up and down. He knew he was going to have so much fun with his new family.

Spot went inside the house and took a look around. He saw a big chair, a soft bed, and some fun toys. Spot played with the toys and ran all around the house. He loved his new home and his new family.

At night, Spot curled up in his soft bed. He was very tired from all the fun he had during the day. He closed his eyes and went to sleep. Spot knew that tomorrow would be another fun day in his new home.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved music and he loved to play the piano. One day, Timmy's mommy took him to the music store to buy a piano. When they arrived, the store owner told them that there were no pianos available to buy. Timmy was sad.

But then, Timmy met a girl named Lily. Lily also loved music and she loved to sing. Timmy and Lily became friends and they played music together. One day, Timmy asked Lily if she wanted to marry him. Lily said yes! Timmy was so happy that he played a song on his imaginary piano for Lily. They lived happily ever after, playing music and singing together.

Once upon a time, there was a number. It was very big and it kept growing. It spread fast and pretty soon it was everywhere. Everyone wanted to know what the number was. Finally, one brave person asked, and the answer came back - it was the number of friends! Everyone was so happy when they heard the answer, and they all shared lots of hugs and smiles. And from then on, the number grew bigger and bigger, spreading fast from one person to another, making lots of happy friends along the way.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they want to talk to their grandma, who lives far away. Grandma has a phone that can show her face and voice. Ben and Lily think this phone is very fun and dependable.

One day, mom says, "Do you want to call grandma? She misses you a lot." Ben and Lily nod and run to the couch. Mom gives them the phone and helps them press the button. Soon, they see grandma's smiling face on the screen.

"Hello, my darlings!" grandma says. "How are you today?"

"We are good, grandma!" Ben says. "We played with blocks and cars and dolls."

"We also read a book about animals, grandma!" Lily says. "We learned about lions and elephants and monkeys."

"That's wonderful, my sweeties!" grandma says. "You are so smart and curious. I'm very proud of you."

Ben and Lily smile and hug the phone. They love their grandma very much. They want to touch her and give her a real hug. But they know they can't do that right now. So they blow her kisses and say, "We love you, grandma!"

"I love you too, my angels!" grandma says. "You make me very happy. I hope to see you soon."

Mom takes the phone and says, "Bye, mom. Thanks for calling. We'll talk to you again later."

"Bye, dear. Take care of yourself and the kids. You're doing a great job." grandma says.

Mom ends the call and puts the phone away. She hugs Ben and Lily and says, "You're very lucky to have such a loving and dependable grandma. She always thinks of you and wants to hear from you."

Ben and Lily nod and say, "We know, mom. We're lucky to have you too. You're the best mom ever."

Mom smiles and says, "Thank you, my loves. You're the best kids ever."

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and a big mattress to jump on. Sometimes they made a fort with the mattress and the blankets and pretended to be pirates or explorers.

One day, their mom told them she had to go to the store and asked them to be good and not make a mess. She said she would be back soon and left them some snacks and juice. Tim and Kim said okay and waved goodbye.

After mom left, Tim and Kim decided to play with the mattress. They dragged it to the middle of the room and started to jump on it. They had fun bouncing and laughing and making silly faces. But then, Tim had an idea.

"Let's make the mattress more fun," he said. "Let's put some juice on it and make it slippery."

Kim thought that was a bad idea. She said, "No, Tim, that's dangerous. We could fall and hurt ourselves. And we could spoil the mattress and make mom angry."

But Tim did not listen. He grabbed a bottle of juice and poured some on the mattress. He said, "Come on, Kim, don't be a baby. It's just juice. It will dry up."

He jumped on the mattress and slid on the juice. He said, "Whee, this is fun. Try it, Kim."

Kim shook her head. She said, "No, Tim, I don't want to. It's not fun, it's stupid. Stop it, Tim, or I'll tell mom."

But Tim did not stop. He poured more juice on the mattress and jumped and slid. He said, "You're no fun, Kim. You're a boring girl. I'm having a blast."

He did not see that the juice was dripping on the floor and making a big puddle. He did not hear that mom was coming back and opening the door. He did not notice that mom was shocked and angry when she saw the mess.

"Tim, Kim, what have you done?" mom yelled. "You spoiled the mattress and the floor. You made a huge mess. You were very naughty and dangerous. How could you do this?"

Tim and Kim stopped jumping and looked at mom. They felt scared and sorry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We were just playing. We didn't mean to spoil the mattress."

Mom sighed. She said, "Playing is good, but you have to be careful and respectful. You have to listen to each other and to me. You have to clean up your mess and apologize. And you have to promise me you will never do this again."

Tim and Kim nodded. They said, "We promise, mom. We're sorry, mom. We love you, mom."

Mom hugged them. She said, "I love you too, Tim and Kim. But you have to learn from your mistakes. Now, let's get some towels and clean this up. And then, you have to go to bed early. No more playing with the mattress today."

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her daughter. The daughter was very sweet and pretty. She loved jam. Every morning, she would help mommy spread jam on her toast.

One day, the girl wanted to make her own jam. She asked mommy to help. Together, they cut up some apples and cooked them on the stove. After awhile, the apples smelled yummy and the jam looked nice.

The girl was so excited, she wanted to give the jam to all of her friends. She put the jam in some jars, but mommy told her that she had better stay home. The girl felt a bit sad, but she knew her mom was right.

When her friends came over, the girl gave each of them a jar of her very own jam. They all said it tasted so yummy and that the girl was very clever. The girl was so proud, she danced around the room.

The jam was always a reminder of the special time that the girl and her mom shared. From then on, the girl always remained happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big comb with pink bristles. Every day, she would comb her hair and make it pretty. One day, her mommy said they were going to drive to the park. Lily was so excited! She loved going to the park to play on the swings and slide. In the car, Lily held onto her comb tightly and looked out the window. When they got to the park, Lily ran to the swings and her mommy pushed her high into the sky. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a squirrel named Sam. Sam loved to play and eat nuts. One day, Sam saw a big, hard nut. He wanted to eat it, but it was too hard to crack open. Sam tried and tried, but he couldn't do it. 

Suddenly, Sam heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a big, black dog rushing towards him! Sam was scared and didn't know what to do. Then, he remembered the hard nut. He quickly grabbed it and ran up a tree. 

The dog tried to climb the tree, but he couldn't. Sam felt safe and ate his nut while watching the dog run away. From that day on, Sam always kept a hard nut with him, just in case he needed to rush away from danger.

Alice was a famous spade digger. Every day she worked hard to dig deep holes in her garden. She loved to use her spade to dig and turn the soil. One day, when Alice was digging in the garden, she found something strange. She carefully pulled the object out of the ground, and it was an old rotting apple. 

"Whoa!" shouted Alice in surprise. She set the apple aside and carried on digging. But the next thing she pulled out of the ground was even more exciting. It was a bone!

Alice ran inside to tell her mum. "Mum," she said, "I found something really cool in the garden!" Her mum laughed and said, "Oh my! That must be something really famous!" 

Alice smiled. She knew that she had found something very special in her garden. She put the bone and the apple in a box and vowed to take good care of them. Alice's garden was full of surprises and she couldn't wait to find out what was buried beneath the earth next.

Just as the little girl was about to reach out and touch it, the shark disappeared deep into the water. She watched it until it was completely gone and she wondered if it would ever reappear. With a smile, the brave little girl slowly returned back to the beach with a magical secret in her mind.

The little boy went over to talk to the youth. He asked him why he was sad. The youth said he had lost his way and didn't know how to get home. The little boy wanted to help, so he offered to walk the youth home.

As they walked, the sun began to set and the light started to fade. They were getting farther away from the little boy's house and he started to feel scared. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and a car came speeding towards them. The little boy tried to push the youth out of the way, but it was too late. The car hit them both and they were hurt very badly.

The little boy's family was very sad when they heard the news. They knew he had been trying to help the youth and they were proud of him. But they were also very sad that he had been hurt. The little boy didn't make it, but his family knew he had died trying to do something good.

Joe was playing in the park one day. He jumped and ran around and noticed a large bubble floating in the air nearby. Joe ran over to the bubble and touched it with his finger. His finger got cold, so he pulled it away. He wondered what could make his finger cold like that.

Joe asked his mom, "What was that cold thing?" His mom smiled. "That was a bubble. We can make more if you want."

Joe was excited. He watched as his mom blew a bubble and floated it into the air. Joe couldn't believe how the bubble moved. He chased the bubble around and laughed loudly. 

Suddenly, Joe noticed the sky had turned grey. His mom said, "I think it's going to rain. We'd better go home now." 

Joe wasn't ready to go home. He still wanted to play with the bubble. But his mom was right, it was starting to rain. Joe reluctantly said goodbye to the bubble and went home with his mom. 

At home, Joe and his mom curled up under a warm blanket and watched the rain outside of the window. Joe saw his bubble again in the rain. It made him smile, because it was still there in the rain, cold and beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to go to the zoo. Her favorite place was the monkey house. The monkeys wore brown coats and rolled around on the ground.

The little girl loved to watch them. She would drop treats into their house and laugh when they would catch them. They looked so happy with their brown coats.

One day, the little girl went to the zoo and it was closed! She was sad but then saw a big box with goodies. The box had her favorite - food for the monkeys! The little girl got so excited, she dropped the box at the door of the monkey house.

The monkeys were so thankful that they danced around the little girl! She was so pleased that she had been able to help her favorite zoo friends. They were having so much fun and enjoying the snacks she had dropped for them.

The little girl left the zoo feeling happy that she had made the monkeys so happy. She would never forget the brown coats and the fun times they shared at the zoo.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Rose. Rose believed in magical things like fairies and dragons.

One day, Rose found a hidden cave. It had a big, dark sink inside. At first, Rose was a bit scared, but then she decided to believe that the sink could be magical.

Rose went to get a special stone that she thought would help her. She closed her eyes and held the stone tight while she wished out loud. Suddenly, the sink started to bubble and sparkle!

Rose opened her eyes and saw that the sink had filled up with bright, glittery water. She put her hand inside, and it felt warm and friendly.

Rose stayed in the hidden cave for a while, playing with her magical sink. Whenever she felt sad, she would go and make a wish in her special sink. With just a little bit of belief, Rose's wishes always seemed to come true. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, she saw her friend Timmy wearing a very cool shirt. 

"Wow, Timmy! That shirt is so cool! Did you design it yourself?" Lily asked.

"Yes, I did! My mom gave me some markers and I drew on the shirt," Timmy replied.

Lily thought that was a great idea. She wanted to design her own shirt too. So, she went home and asked her mom if she could have a plain white shirt. Her mom gave her one and Lily drew all over it with her markers.

The next day, Lily wore her new shirt to play with her friends. They all thought it was very cool and normal. They played in the sun all day and had lots of fun. The end.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom was a happy boy who liked to play all day. One day, Tom met a new friend, Sam. They decided to play outside together.

As they played, Tom said, "Sam, tomorrow is an important day. We will have a big party in the park." Sam was excited and said, "I can't wait for the party, Tom!"

The next day, the sun shone brightly as the party began. Tom and Sam played games and ate yummy food. Suddenly, the wind began to blow hard, and it started to rain. Tom and Sam ran under a tree for shelter. Tom said, "Don't worry, Sam. We can still have fun."

They played under the tree until the rain stopped. When the sun came out again, they continued to enjoy the important day. Tom and Sam were very happy they could still have fun, even when the rain tried to ruin their day. They knew they would always remember this special day.

Jill and Ben were bored. It was a gloomy day and they could not go outside. They looked around the house for something fun to do.

"Look, there is a frame on the wall," Jill said. "It has a picture of a dog."

"Let's see it," Ben said. He climbed on a chair and reached for the frame. He tried to pull it off the wall, but it was stuck.

"Be careful, Ben," Jill said. "You might break it."

But Ben pulled harder and harder. He wanted to see the dog. Suddenly, the frame came off the wall and fell on the floor. It made a loud noise and the glass broke.

"Oh no!" Jill and Ben said. They were scared. They heard their mom coming.

"What was that?" their mom asked. She saw the broken frame and the picture of the dog. She was angry.

"Who did this?" she asked.

Jill and Ben looked at each other. They did not want to get in trouble. They did not know what to say. They wished they had not pulled the frame.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful elderly lady who was walking in the park. She saw a hive buzzing with bees in a tree and she knew she needed to be careful. She slowly moved closer and saw something small on the ground. After taking a closer look she noticed it was a tear. She smiled as she recognised it as a bee tear.

The elderly lady carefully picked up the bee tear and looked around for the bee that had dropped it. She saw a cute bee buzzing around and flew towards the hive.

The bee tear made the elderly woman feel kind and she decided to give the bee a hug. She stepped closer, carefully so as not to disturb the hive, and hugged the bee. The bee smiled and flew away happily.

The elderly lady smiled as the bee flew away, feeling like the hug had helped the bee in some way. She looked up at the hive, feeling happy that the bees were safe.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play with their dog, Rex. Rex is a big, black lab. He is very friendly and smart.

One day, Sam and Ben find a big box in the garage. It has many wires and buttons and lights. They do not know what it is. They think it is a toy.

"Let's play with it!" Sam says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They open the box and see a big machine. It has a screen and a keyboard and a microphone. They see words on the screen. They do not know what they mean.

"Maybe it can talk to us!" Ben says.

"Let's try!" Sam says.

They press some buttons and speak into the microphone. They say hello and their names and ask questions. They wait for the machine to answer.

But the machine does not answer. It makes a loud noise and sparks. The screen goes black. The machine is broken.

Sam and Ben are scared. They run away from the box. They find Rex in the living room. He is sleeping on the couch. He hears them and opens his eyes. He sees them and wags his tail.

"Rex, Rex, we are sorry!" Sam says.

"We did something bad!" Ben says.

They hug Rex and tell him what they did. Rex listens and yawns. He does not care about the box. He cares about his boys. He licks their faces and makes them laugh.

"Rex, you are the best!" Sam says.

"Rex, you are smarter than us!" Ben says.

They play with Rex and forget about the box. They do not know that the box is their dad's computer. He uses it for his work. He is a scientist. He will be very angry when he sees what they did. He will think they are foolish. But Rex will not. He will love them anyway.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends saw a big pile of hay. They wanted to play on it, but it was too high. 

Lily's friend, Emily, said, "I wish we could slide down the hay like a slide." 

Lily had an idea. She ran to her house and came back with a helpful tool - a big piece of cardboard. They put the cardboard on the hay and slid down. It was so much fun! 

After playing for a while, they heard a loud noise. It was the farmer who owned the hay. He said, "What are you doing on my hay?" 

Lily said, "We're sorry. We just wanted to play." 

The farmer smiled and said, "I remember when I was your age. I used to play on hay too. But next time, ask me first." From that day on, they always asked the farmer before playing on his hay.

Lily liked to play with her dad's office things. She liked the pens, the papers, the stapler and the calculator. She liked to pretend she was working like her dad. Sometimes, her dad let her sit on his lap and help him with his work.

One day, her dad had a very important work to do. He had to complete a report for his boss. He told Lily he needed to focus and not to disturb him. Lily nodded and said she would be quiet. She took some papers and pens and went to the corner of the office. She wanted to make her own report.

She drew some pictures and wrote some words. She used the stapler to put the papers together. She used the calculator to make some numbers. She was very proud of her report. She wanted to show it to her dad.

She walked to her dad's desk and said, "Dad, look at my report. I completed it for you." She put her report on top of his report. Her dad looked at her report and smiled. He said, "Wow, Lily, this is a very nice report. You did a great job. Thank you for helping me."

He hugged her and kissed her. He said, "But you know, this is my report. I need to send it to my boss. Your report is very pretty, but it is not what my boss wants. And you used some of my expensive papers and pens. Those are for special work only. Next time, please ask me before you use them, okay?"

Lily felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, dad. I didn't know. I just wanted to make you happy. Can I keep my report?" Her dad said, "Of course, you can keep your report. It is yours. And you made me very happy. I love you, Lily. But now, I need to finish my report. Can you play with something else for a while?"

Lily said, "Okay, dad. I love you too. I will play with something else." She took her report and went to the corner of the office. She found some toys and books. She played with them quietly. She was happy. She had completed her report. And her dad had liked it.

Sara loved to sleep with her teddy bear. She hugged him every night and told him stories. Teddy was her best friend. But one day, Sara's mom said they had to go on a trip. She said they would be gone for a long time. Sara looked at the calendar on the wall. It had many red marks on it. Mom said each mark was a day they would be away.

Sara felt sad. She did not want to leave Teddy. She asked Mom if she could take him with her. Mom said no. She said Teddy was too big and there was not enough room in the suitcase. She said Teddy would be safe and happy at home. She said Sara could call him on the phone sometimes.

Sara did not like this. She cried and hugged Teddy. She said she would miss him a lot. She said she was sorry. Teddy looked at her with his big brown eyes. He said he would miss her too. He said he was not sorry. He said he was proud of her. He said she was brave and smart and kind. He said he would wait for her to come back. He said he loved her.

Sara smiled and kissed Teddy. She said she loved him too. She said she would call him every day. She said she would tell him about the trip. She said she would bring him a gift. She said he was the best teddy bear in the world.

Sara and Mom packed their bags and got in the car. Sara waved goodbye to Teddy. Teddy waved back. He watched them drive away. He felt sad, but he also felt happy. He knew Sara would have fun and learn new things. He knew she would come back soon. He knew they would sleep together again. He closed his eyes and dreamed of Sara.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Joy. She had a big backyard. The backyard was very safe and perfect for her to play.

Every day, Joy liked to play outside. She liked to run, swing, and explore. One day, Joy decided to load her red wagon with a few toys from the backyard. She filled it with soft dolls and colorful balls. She was so excited to take her wagon outside.

Once she was done loading the wagon, Joy pulled it to the park. She sang and laughed as she walked along the path. She explored every corner of the park.

After a long day of exploring, Joy loaded her wagon with toys and took it back to her backyard. She was tired, but she was very happy. Her backyard was so safe and so much fun.

The End.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Jack. He was only three years old, but he was very curious. He wanted to know about everything around him.

One day, Jack found an axe in the forest. He had never seen an axe before, and he was very surprised. But he was also a bit scared.

Suddenly, he heard a voice call to him from the tree. "Listen," said the voice, "I'll tell you about this axe. It can be used to chop wood and make kindling." Jack listened closely and thought about what the voice had said.

The next day, Jack went back to the forest with some kindling. He was thoughtful, and he knew how to use the axe safely. He made a fire and was able to keep warm as he cooked dinner.

Jack smiled to himself as he felt a sense of satisfaction. He had been very brave and very thoughtful. He was proud of himself.

Once there was a seed. It wanted to grow and be very big. So it used its tool and dug into the ground. Every day it worked harder and harder. Pretty soon, it had become very high.

But then the wind came by. The wind blew and blew and blew. It blew so hard that the seed fell down. It had grown so tall that it couldn't stay standing any longer.

The seed was sad. It had worked so hard, but still it had not grown big. Then it realized that it should have stayed small. The seed never grew again.

Once upon a time a man was walking through the woods. He had been warned to be careful becasue he was close to a big pit. As he walked he saw a reliable animal in the thicket. It was a furry, brown bear.

The man was scared but the bear didn't seem to notice him. He stood motionless and the bear just stared at him. It was still and its face was soft. The man was relieved and kept walking through the woods. He remembered the warning and kept away from the pit.

He eventually made it through the woods safely and looked back on what had happened. He was happy he had trusted his instinct and listened to the warning. It had kept him away from the pit and made him feel safe.

The man was so thankful to be reliable and cautious. He went home happy and well. The end.

Once upon a time there was a white bird named True. True was a very special bird who liked to collect things. He would collect colorful feathers, twigs, and pebbles.

One day, True found a white feather. It was so beautiful that he decided to collect it. True flew all around looking for more, but he just couldnâ€™t find any. But then he discovered something special - a white rock!

True collected the rock and took it back to his nest. He kept it there and looked at it every day. True was so proud of his white rock!

The rock made True very happy, and he always kept it close. True and the rock were the best of friends.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved waffles. Every morning, her mother would make her a big waffle for breakfast. One day, Lily's mother said, "Lily, I have a surprise for you. We're going to visit Grandma today and she has a special waffle recipe."

Lily was so excited to try Grandma's waffles. As they drove to Grandma's house, Lily saw a big scary tree. She said, "Mommy, that tree looks frightened." Her mother said, "Don't worry, it's just an old tree."

When they arrived at Grandma's house, Lily saw a big present wrapped in colorful paper. She asked, "What's in the present?" Grandma said, "It's a surprise for later."

After breakfast, Lily opened the present and inside was a waffle maker. She was so happy and couldn't wait to make waffles with her mom. As they made waffles, Lily remembered the frightened tree and said, "Mommy, I'm not frightened anymore. I have you and my waffle maker to make me happy."

One day, Timmy and his sister Sally went outside to play in the snow. They made a big snowman and threw snowballs at each other. Suddenly, Timmy saw a big hill covered in snow.

"I dare you to slide down the hill with me!" Timmy said to Sally.

Sally was scared, but she wanted to be brave like her brother. "Okay, I'll try," she said.

They slid down the hill together, laughing and screaming. When they got to the bottom, Sally said, "That was so much fun! Do you want to do it again?"

But Timmy shook his head. "I can't, I have to go inside. Mom said dinner is available now."

Sally nodded and they went inside, happy and tired from their snowy adventure.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jenny. She was very troubled and had many worries. One day, she decided to go for a walk in the park. 

When she arrived she was amazed to find a big fountain in the middle. All around there were beautiful pink and white flowers. Jenny was surprised and happy to find such a nice place. She started to relax and forget about her troubles.

Suddenly, she heard music coming from the fountain. It was playing a magical and joyful song, like nothing she had ever heard before. Jenny began to dance and twirl around the fountain, feeling more and more happy. 

Then, a small fairy appeared. She said, â€œI'm here to provide you with joy and happinessâ€. She waved her wand in the air and immediately the fountain started to spray out thousands of colourful bubbles. 

Jenny was so happy and excited. She waved goodbye to the magical fairy and ran around the park, feeling lighter than air. From that day onwards, every time she felt troubled, she always returned to the fountain to be reminded of the special magical gift the fairy provided her.

Tommy was a lonely boy. He had no friends to play with at school. He liked to draw and read, but the other kids said he was boring. Tommy wished he had someone who liked him.

One day, he saw a new girl in his class. Her name was Lily. She had a big smile and a pink backpack. Tommy wanted to talk to her, but he was shy. He thought she would not like him either.

At recess, Tommy sat on a bench and watched Lily play with a ball. She looked happy and fun. Tommy felt sad. He wished he had a ball too. He looked in his backpack and found a crayon and a paper. He decided to draw a ball for himself.

He was so busy drawing that he did not notice Lily coming to him. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. What are you doing?"

Tommy looked up and saw her. He felt nervous. He said, "Hi, I'm Tommy. I'm drawing a ball."

Lily smiled and said, "That's a nice ball. Can I see it?"

Tommy nodded and gave her his paper. Lily looked at it and said, "Wow, you are good at drawing. I like your ball. Can I draw with you?"

Tommy felt surprised and happy. He said, "Sure, you can. I have a crayon. Do you want to use it?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. Thank you for sharing. What do you want to draw?"

Tommy thought for a moment and said, "How about a toe?"

Lily laughed and said, "A toe? That's funny. Why a toe?"

Tommy said, "Because toes are funny and cute. And because I have to use the word toe in my story."

Lily said, "What story?"

Tommy said, "The story I'm writing for my homework. We have to use the words supply, toe, and lonely in a story."

Lily said, "That sounds hard. Can I help you?"

Tommy said, "Yes, you can. That would be nice. Maybe we can write a story about us."

Lily said, "That sounds fun. Let's do it."

Tommy and Lily started to write their story together. They used the crayon and the paper as their supply. They wrote about how they met and how they became friends. They wrote about how they drew a toe and how they laughed. They wrote about how they were not lonely anymore.

They finished their story and read it aloud. They smiled and hugged. They said, "We like our story. We like each other. We are friends."

The moral of the story is: You can find a friend if you are kind and share. You can have fun if you are creative and curious. You can use simple words to make a good story.

Once there was a new gorilla. He was walking around the jungle happily. Then he saw another gorilla teasing him. The new gorilla got angry and ran towards the teasing gorilla. They started to fight and soon the entire jungle was filled with laughter. Everyone was cheering them on. The new gorilla was finally stronger and he managed to win the fight. After the fight finished, the new gorilla was feeling pleased with himself and went off in search of new adventures.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved music and playing her violin. Everywhere she went, she would take her violin and play with it. Everywhere, that is, until one day she stumbled upon a yummy looking apple tree. She had never seen anything so yummy before and all she wanted to do was reach up and pick an apple.

Lucy asked her mom, "Mom can I pick the apple?" Her mom said, "No, Lucy, it's not safe, it might not be yummy." But Lucy was so excited, she wanted to pick the apple so badly and so finally, her mom said, "Okay, but be careful."

Lucy reached up and plucked the apple from the tree and took her first bite. It was even yummier than she thought! She was so happy and started singing and dancing and playing her violin. She was so caught up in the moment that she didn't realize the apple tree was growing bigger and bigger. 

Suddenly, the apple tree had grown so big and out of control she couldn't move! She tried to call for help, but no one could hear her. She was trapped there until the end of time, playing her violin. 

The moral of the story is that although something might look yummy at first, it may not be safe and it may lead to a bad ending.

Lily and Tom are playing in the living room. They have many toys on the floor. Mom comes in and sees the mess. She is not happy.

"Look at this, Lily and Tom. You need to tidy up your toys. It is almost time for dinner," Mom says.

"But we are having fun, Mom. Can we play a little more?" Lily asks.

"No, you have played enough. Now you need to help me. Put your toys in the box, please," Mom says.

Lily and Tom start to pick up their toys. They put them in the box one by one. Mom points to a bowl on the table.

"What is that, Mom?" Tom asks.

"That is a bowl of soup. I made it for dinner. It is very yummy. Do you want some?" Mom asks.

"Yes, please. I like soup," Tom says.

"Me too. I like soup," Lily says.

"Good. Then hurry up and finish tidying up. Then you can wash your hands and come to the table," Mom says.

Lily and Tom finish tidying up. They are proud of their work. The living room looks nice and clean. They wash their hands and go to the table. Mom gives them each a bowl of soup and a spoon. They eat their soup and enjoy it.

"Thank you, Mom. The soup is very yummy," Lily and Tom say.

"You are welcome, Lily and Tom. I am glad you like it. And thank you for tidying up your toys. You are very good helpers," Mom says.

Lily and Tom smile. They are happy. They love their mom and their soup.

One day, Jack and Jill went for a walk in the park. They were talking about different things and having fun. Suddenly, a taxi stopped in front of them. It was a yellow taxi and it was very shiny. Jack was very curious about the taxi and he asked Jill, "What is that?" Jill smiled and said "It's a taxi". Jack's eyes were wide open with excitement and he asked "Can we get in it?" Jill laughed and said "Maybe! Let's go and ask the driver".

They went up to the driver and Jack asked him: "Can we get a ride?". The driver looked at them, smiling and said "Sure! Where do you two want to go?". Jack was so excited. He told the driver their address and the driver agreed.

When they were in the taxi, Jack asked Jill all sorts of questions. He was really curious about how the taxi works. Jill discussed each of the questions with Jack, slowly and gently. Finally, they arrived at their destination. They thanked the driver and hopped out of the taxi.

Jack and Jill enjoyed their ride. From then on, Jack always talked about the taxi whenever he saw one. He was so curious and he loved to discuss it with everyone!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She loved to skip. Every day she'd put on her shoes and go skipping around the garden.

One day, Lucy found a box filled with salt. She thought it was really hard to carry, but she decided to take it anyway.

Suddenly, Lucy started feeling funny in her stomach. She wanted to skip but it was too hard to do with a big box of salt.

So, Lucy looked around to find something to help her. She saw a stick and had a brilliant idea. She put the box of salt on the stick and lifted it up.

Lucy smiled as she carried and skipped around the garden. She had solved her problem and she was very happy.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who lived in a happy house. One day, they decided to go outside and find something to do. As they looked around, they noticed a big rock.

"Wow!" said one friend to the other, "that rock sure is big. What should we do with it?"

The other friend thought for a moment, then had a great idea. "Let's add some cheerful colors to the rock!" she said excitedly. 

The friends then took out a bunch of paint. They added lovely colors to the rock and made it a work of art. When they were finished, the friends stepped back to admire their work. 

The cheerful colors made the rock even more beautiful. Both friends smiled and hugged each other to show their happiness. 

They then decided they had found the perfect thing to do and they ran back to their happy house, ready to tell their families all about it.

Sammy had a big day ahead. He was playing his first game of pitch. 

Ahead of the game, he ran around excitedly, smiling in the light sunshine. His family was all around, cheering him on. They had been practicing in the backyard for weeks, dropping the ball into the pitch. 

Then, the game started. Everyone was watching Sammy, waiting for the pitch. He thought about the weeks he's been practicing with his family, feeling confident even though he was a little nervous. 

The pitch came and Sammy dropped the ball. He watched it roll into the pitch and he cheered. 

Everyone cheered with him and his family congratulated him. Sammy felt so happy that he could share such a special moment with them. He couldn't wait to go home and tell his friends.

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He was a very shy boy and never wanted to talk to anyone. One day, his mommy had a great idea! She told him he should go outside and play with some of the other kids. Joe was scared, but he wanted to have fun.

So, he bravely stepped outside and saw some of his school friends. They waved to him and asked him to come play with them. Joe was very shy, but he was also curious. He slowly started walking towards them.

Suddenly, Joe tripped and fell to the ground. He was embarrassed and wanted to hide. But then the other kids started laughing and it made him feel better. Now they were all playing together and Joe was having so much fun. 

The idea of having fun outside made Joe feel much more brave. He wasn't so shy anymore and was even suggesting ideas to the group. It was a wonderful day and Joe was so glad that he had gone outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, she saw her little brother crying because he didn't have a cushion to sit on. She felt sad for him and decided to help.

Lily went to her room and found a cushion. She brought it to her brother and he was very happy. He thanked her and gave her a big hug. Lily felt proud of herself for being able to supply her brother with what he needed.

Later that day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her toys. Lily didn't want to do it because she was tired. But then she remembered how happy she made her brother by supplying him with a cushion. She realized that doing things for others can make them happy.

From that day on, Lily made sure to help her family whenever she could. She learned that being kind and helpful is never disgusting, but always the right thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pippin. Pippin loved to play with his friends and slide on the icy ground. One day, Pippin noticed that the world was getting colder and colder. He felt sad because his friends were starting to leave and go somewhere else. 

Pippin's mom told him that soon the world would settle into winter, and that it would be very icy. Pippin didn't know what that meant, but he trusted his mom. 

As the days went by, Pippin noticed that the ground was getting harder and harder. He started to slip and slide, but he didn't mind because he was having fun. Then one day, Pippin's mom told him it was time to go. Pippin didn't want to leave, but he knew he had to. 

When Pippin and his family arrived at their new home, Pippin was surprised to see that everything was covered in snow and ice. He realized that his mom was right, the world had settled into winter and it was very icy. But Pippin wasn't scared anymore, he was excited to explore his new icy world with his family.

Once upon a time there was a silly little girl who was always making funny faces. She would make faces when she was eating her breakfast, when she was playing with her toys, and even when she was asleep. She was known for her funny frowns and everyone around her found it so amusing. 

One day, when the girl was about to take her afternoon nap, an alarm suddenly went off. It was a rare kind of alarm that none of us had heard before. We all stood still, unsure of what to do. 

But then the silly little girl put on her best frown and shouted â€œI know what to do!â€ She hopped out of bed and headed straight towards the alarm. She grabbed it with both hands and shook it until it stopped making noise. Everyone cheered at her brave act, and even the alarm seemed to smile. 

The little girl was proud of her accomplishment and she had a huge smile on her face. From that day forward, no one ever had to worry about the rare alarm again. 

The End.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play at the park. They like to swing and climb and slide. One day, they find a shiny penny on the ground. Anna picks it up and shows it to Ben.

"Look, I have a penny!" she says. "It is so pretty and round. I can buy candy with it."

Ben feels jealous. He wants the penny too. He thinks it is not fair that Anna has it. He tries to grab it from her hand. Anna pulls it back and says, "No, it is mine! I found it first. You cannot have it."

They start to fight over the penny. They tug and pull and shout. They forget to play and have fun. They make each other sad and angry.

A lady sees them and comes over. She is kind and gentle. She says, "What is wrong, children? Why are you fighting?"

Anna and Ben tell her about the penny. They both want it. They both think they deserve it.

The lady smiles and says, "I have an idea. Why don't you share the penny? You can take turns holding it and looking at it. You can also use it to play a game. You can flip it and see if it lands on heads or tails. You can slide it across the slide and see how far it goes. You can make a wish and toss it in the fountain. There are many ways to enjoy the penny together."

Once upon a time, there was a generous family. They had a tall tree in their garden and they loved the windy days that blew around it. The family enjoyed their windy days so much that they moved the tree to the front of the house so they could see it turn even more. What a generous family! They were always grateful for the gifts the wind gave them!

The sun was setting on a warm summer evening. Sam and Bella were sitting on their porch, discussing their plans for the evening. Sam wanted to stay home and play with his toys, but Bella wanted to do something more adventurous.

"Let's explore the forest," said Bella.

Sam was very excited. "We can climb trees and look for bugs and birds!" he said.

So Sam and Bella put on their shoes and grabbed a flashlight. They opened the door to the forest, and soon they were exploring in the darkness. They heard crickets chirping and the breeze rustling through the trees.

They discovered so many new things. They saw a groundhog and a fox and even an owl! Sam and Bella had the most adventurous and exciting evening.  When it was time to go home, they both agreed that exploring the forest was the best idea ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very fancy. She always wanted to park in style. So one day, the little girl packed a picnic and found a very special place to park.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little boy called Tim. He wanted to find something special and so he decided to go on an adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Max. He wanted to go on a trip with his family, but he was very tired. So he stayed home alone.

Once upon a time, there was a big fat body. It was so big and fat that it couldn't fit through the door! But this body was happy, because it loved to splash in the water.

One sunny day, it decided to go to the beach. It had a big smile on its face as it waddled over to the sea. When it got to the water, it dipped its toes in and felt the coolness of the water.

"Hurray!", the body yelled and splashed in the waves. It jumped up and down and laughed and shouted. After a while, it looked up and saw a little girl about three years old. The little girl was standing right next to the body and had a big, wide grin on her face.

"Are you having fun?", the little girl asked the body. The body smiled and said, "Yes, I am having so much fun! Do you want to splash with me?" 

The little girl nodded happily and started to splash in the water. Both of them splashed and laughed and had a great time. When the sun went down, the little girl and the body said goodbye and went home with big smiles on their faces.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. They were having fun. But then they saw a big dog. The dog was black and had sharp teeth. The dog was barking and running towards them.

"Help!" Tim shouted. "The dog is scary!"

Mia was brave. She picked up a stick and waved it at the dog. "Go away, dog!" she said. "We don't want to play with you!"

But the dog did not listen. The dog was angry and powerful. The dog jumped and bit Mia's arm. Mia cried out in pain. She dropped the stick and fell to the ground.

Tim ran to Mia. He saw blood on her arm. He was scared and sad. He wanted to help Mia. He took his shirt and tried to wipe the blood. But the blood did not stop. He did not know what to do.

"Tim, I'm hungry," Mia said. "Can we have a snack?"

Tim looked at Mia. He saw her eyes were closing. He knew she was very sick. He wished he had a snack for her. He wished he had a phone to call for help. He wished the dog was gone. But he had nothing. He could only hug Mia and cry.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to eat yummy treats and run around in the grass. One day, Spot saw a big bone on the ground and he wanted to eat it. But the bone was too big for him to carry in his mouth. 

Spot saw a bigger dog and asked him, "Can you help me carry this bone?" The bigger dog answered, "Yes, I can help you." The bigger dog picked up the bone with his heel and carried it to Spot's house. 

Spot was very happy and thanked the bigger dog. He learned that it's important to ask for help when you need it. And it's also important to answer when someone asks you for help. From that day on, Spot and the bigger dog became good friends and shared yummy treats together.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he was playing with his favorite red truck when it got stuck in a box.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Bertha. She was three years old, and loved to play outside. One day, Bertha decided to explore the woods. While she was walking, she found a purple flower. It was very clean, so she decided to pick it.

Suddenly, a big bird came flying. He looked angry and he told Bertha, â€œHey, give back the flower! Itâ€™s mine!â€ Bertha hugged the flower tightly and said, â€œNo, I wonâ€™t give it back!â€
