Lily loved to play with her colorful blocks. She liked to stack them high and make towers and castles. She had many blocks of different shapes and sizes. She was very proud of her blocks.

One day, Lily's big brother Tom came into her room. He saw her blocks and wanted to play with them too. He did not ask Lily. He just took some of her blocks and made his own tower. Lily was angry. She said, "Those are my blocks! Give them back!" But Tom did not listen. He said, "I am bigger than you. I can play with whatever I want." He took more of her blocks and made his tower taller and taller.

Lily tried to get her blocks back, but Tom pushed her away. He said, "Go away, you little baby. You don't need so many blocks. You can play with something else." He laughed and made his tower even higher. Lily felt sad and mad. She wished she could make Tom's tower disappear.

Then, she had an idea. She saw her mom's iron on the table. She knew that the iron made steam when it was hot. She also knew that steam was like water, but very hot and thin. She thought, "Maybe if I make steam near Tom's tower, it will make his blocks wet and soft. Then his tower will fall down and he will be sorry."

She waited until Tom was not looking. She turned on the iron and moved it close to Tom's tower. She saw the steam coming out of the iron. She smiled and said, "Bye bye, tower!"

But Lily did not know that the iron was very dangerous. The steam was not only hot and thin, but also fast and strong. It did not make Tom's blocks wet and soft. It made them fly away and disappear. It also made the iron fall off the table and hit the floor. The floor made a loud noise and the iron made a big spark.

Tom and Lily were both scared. They screamed and ran out of the room. Their mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the iron, the spark, and the missing blocks. She was very angry and worried. She said, "What did you do? You could have started a fire! You could have hurt yourselves! You are both in big trouble!"

Tom and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They realized that they were both wrong. Tom was wrong to take Lily's blocks and be mean to her. Lily was wrong to use the iron and try to ruin Tom's tower. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were not nice to each other. We did not think about the iron. We will not do it again."

Their mom hugged them and said, "I am glad you are sorry. I love you both. But you have to be careful and respectful. You have to ask before you use someone else's things. You have to share and play nicely. You have to stay away from things that can hurt you. You have to learn from your mistakes."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We will, mom. We will." They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry, too. We love you, too." They went to look for their blocks. They hoped they could find them and make new towers together. They learned that being selfish and sneaky can make things disappear, but being kind and honest can make things better.

Nina was playing tag with her friends when she noticed a shiny diamond on the ground. Her eyes lit up as she ran over to it, knelt down and picked it up. The diamond was so big and sparkly that Nina couldn't believe she had found it.

When she tried to hold onto the diamond, she realised that it was stuck in the ground. She pushed and pulled with all her might, but the diamond wouldn't budge.

"Please come out," Nina said. "I want to take you home!"

Nina struggled for a long time, but she couldn't get the diamond out. Then her friend Jack came over.

"Let me help," he said.

He grabbed a stick from the ground and started to dig. After a few minutes, the diamond was free.

"Wow!" said Nina.

"It wasn't so hard, was it?" Jack said with a grin. "Now it's easy to take it home."

Nina was so excited that she couldn't stop smiling. She thanked Jack and then quickly ran home with her treasure.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Jane. Tom liked to climb, but his friend Jane was scared of heights. Tom knew Jane was scared so he always stayed far away from fences. One day, the friends went to a park near the house. Suddenly, Tom saw a fence that was very high. He couldn't resist, and he started to climb. 

Jane saw this and became nervous.She ran to the fence and said to Tom, 'Stop! It's too dangerous!' But Tom didn't listen. Jane tried to prevent Tom from climbing the fence, but it was too late.

Tom kept climbing and eventually reached the top. He was amazed at how high he was! As Tom looked around, he saw just how risky it was to climb the fence. He realized that Jane was right - he shouldn't have climbed it!

The moral of the story is that it is important to be careful when you are doing something that can be dangerous, and to listen to people who know better. It is always better to be safe than sorry!

Once upon a time, there was a little boat that loved to sail. The boat had fur on its sail. It was the original boat with fur.

One day, while the boat was sailing, it met another boat. The other boat did not have fur on its sail. The other boat said, "I want fur like you."

The two boats tried to share the fur, but it was not enough. The original boat with fur was sad. It wanted to make the other boat happy.

Then, the wind blew the fur from the original boat's sail. The fur split into two pieces. Now, both boats had fur on their sails. They were happy and sailed together in the sea.

One day, an elderly man was walking in the park. He spotted something shiny and twinkling in the grass. It was a can of spray! He was tempted to take it but he was an old man and thought it was wrong. 

He continued his stroll but eventually stopped at a lonely yarn shop. He entered and the shopkeeper handed him the can of spray he saw in the park. As the shopkeeper handed it over, his face became cold and sly. 

The old man thought it was weird, but he took the can anyway. As soon as he got home, he decided to try it out and sprayed the can everywhere. But unfortunately, the spray was poisonous and the old man was very ill. 

The elderly man had been set up by the shopkeeper. The shopkeeper knew of the old man's temptation of the spray in the park and gave it to him to fulfill his desire, but the old man had no idea of the consequences.

One day, Jenny was very weak. She wanted to do something fun so she went outside. When she was outside, she saw something exciting! She saw a gumball machine! Jenny wanted to try it and see if she could get a gumball. She put a coin in the machine and pulled the handle. With a big spring, out popped a pink gumball! 

Jenny excitedly took the gumball, unwrapped it and put it in her mouth. It was so sweet and chewy that it put a smile on her face! She was very happy and went around the playground to show all of her friends her colorful gumball.

Jenny continued to play until she started to feel weak again. She went home and took a nap. She was so glad that her gumball made her day just a little bit better!

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a big van. He was very busy driving his van all around town. He sold ice cream from his van and lots of people liked to buy it.

From that day on, the man was always very busy driving his van and selling ice cream. And everyone was happy because they could buy yummy ice cream from him.

Once upon a time, there was a small white bird. The bird wanted to go out and explore the world. 

Today was a special day and the bird wanted to suggest something to his friends. He said, "Let's go on an adventure! It will be fun!"

His friends were excited. They grabbed their coats and followed the white bird out the door.

They scampered through the woods and explored the valley. They were so busy they didn't notice the sun was setting. 

Suddenly, they heard the bird say, "Let's go home. It's too dark outside." His friends agreed and they all trotted back to their nest. 

The white bird had a big smile on his face. His plan for an adventure had been a success!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Tam. She was 3 years old and very curious. She was always asking questions and wanted to know more about the world.

One day, Tam asked her mom for a new cell phone. Her mom said no, and told her that she was too young to have a cell phone. Tam was very disappointed.

Later that day, Tam's mom talked to her and said, "I have an idea that might be better than a cell phone. We could get you a modern toy instead!" Tam was excited.

The next day, Tam's mom took her to the toy store and Tam saw a beautiful playhouse. It was modern and very colorful. Tam's mom recommended it to her and said it would help her use her imagination and learn new things.

Tam was very happy with her new toy and she loved to play with it. She learned a lot of things from it and enjoyed her new playhouse more than she would have enjoyed a new cell phone.

The moral of this story is to remember that traditional toys can be very educational and fun!

Michael toddled around the playground, admiring the colorful slides and swings. He was determined to try each one. As he walked, he stumbled over a rock. Michael fell onto the ground. He started to cry.

Suddenly, his mom heard the cries and ran to him. "Oh no! Are you okay?" His mom asked.

Michael sniffled and pointed to his toe. "It hurts," he cried.

His mom looked closer and saw a tiny cut on his toe. "It's okay, let's get you some help," she said, picking him up.

Inside the house, his mom got out a bandage and began wrapping it around Michael's toe. He grasped at the bandage and tried to rip it off.

"Michael, it's important to keep the bandage on," his mom said. She was very persistent.

Michael stopped for a moment and slowly nodded. He knew his mum was right, so he held on until the bandage was securely in place. Now his boo-boo was safe. He smiled and hugged his mom.

Once upon a time there lived a sweet little caterpillar called Fluffy. Fluffy loved to explore the world and was always on the lookout for something new.

The butterfly said "Thank you for joining me on this adventure. I have one more thing for you to take home - a sweet, sweet treat".

Fluffy was delighted. He thanked the butterfly for such an amazing experience. He then ran home with the treat in hand, ready to show his family what a wonderful day he'd had.

Mummy made a new dress for Sophie. She tried it on and it fitted perfectly! She was so happy that she jumped up and down.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to go to the park to play with his friends. One day, while he was playing, he saw a vendor selling balloons. Timmy really wanted a balloon, but he didn't have any money.

Timmy felt sad and started to cry. Suddenly, a kind lady saw him crying and came to hug him. She asked Timmy why he was crying and he told her about the balloon. The lady gave Timmy a big hug and bought him a balloon.

Timmy was so happy that he ran back to his friends to show them his new balloon. But when he got there, he saw that one of his friends had popped his balloon. Timmy felt angry and sad again. But then, his friend came to him and gave him a big hug, saying sorry for popping his balloon.

Timmy felt better and hugged his friend back. He learned that even though bad things can happen, hugs can make everything feel light and better again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park to play with her friends. One day, she saw a pony in the park. Lily was so excited to see the pony, and she wanted to pet it. 

Lily went to the pony and said, "Hi, pony! Can I pet you?" The pony said, "Yes, you can pet me, but be careful. My tail is bitter." Lily didn't understand what the pony meant, but she wanted to pet it anyway. 

Lily reached out to pet the pony's tail, and she pulled it. The pony jumped and said, "Ouch! I told you my tail is bitter!" Lily felt bad for hurting the pony, and she apologized. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be careful around the pony and never pulled its tail again.

The boy was very busy. He always had something to do. Today he had a special task. He had to match the ceiling. He found some papers with pictures on them and he matched them to the ceiling. He looked up and the ceiling had changed! It was brighter and more colourful! He was really happy and proud of his work.

The boy was so busy matching the ceiling that he didn't notice his mom come in until she said, "Wow! You're so busy!" The boy smiled and said, "I finished matching the ceiling!" His mom said, "That's great! You did a wonderful job."

The boy was so proud of his work. He felt like a grownup! He had done something he never thought he could do. He had matched the ceiling and made his room look brighter and more colourful. He was happy and couldn't wait to show his friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived on a farm with her family. They grew wheat on the farm. One day, Lily was excited to help her family turn the wheat. She loved to play in the fields and watch the wheat sway in the wind.

As they were turning the wheat, Lily saw a little bird. The bird was chirping and hopping around in the wheat. Lily got so excited that she ran towards the bird. But as she got closer, she accidentally stepped on the wheat and damaged it.

Lily felt very sad because she had ruined the wheat. Her family was upset too because they needed the wheat to make bread. They had to throw away all the damaged wheat and had no bread to eat. Lily learned that it's important to be careful and not to get too excited sometimes.

Anna and Ben were playing in the yard. They had a big pile of leaves that they raked with their rake. They liked to jump in the leaves and make them fly in the air.

"Look at me, Anna!" Ben said. "I can do a flip in the leaves!"

Ben ran and jumped and did a flip. He landed on his back in the leaves. He smiled and laughed.

"You are so good, Ben!" Anna said. "You are graceful like a bird!"

Anna wanted to try too. She ran and jumped and did a flip. But she did not land in the leaves. She landed in a puddle of water. She got wet and cold. She cried and shivered.

"Oh no, Anna!" Ben said. "You are soaked! You need a towel and a hug!"

Ben ran to the house and got a towel. He wrapped it around Anna and gave her a hug. He said he was sorry for the puddle.

"It's okay, Ben," Anna said. "It was an accident. You are a good brother."

They went inside the house and had some hot cocoa. They were happy and warm. They still liked to play in the leaves, but they watched out for puddles.

Mum and her little girl were making ice cream. The girl watched as Mum filled the bowl with cream and sugar. She smiled as Mum put it in the big box that shook and turned it around.

"What's that called, Mum?" the little girl asked.

"It's an ice cream maker," said Mum. "And do you know what it does?"

The little girl shook her head.

"It melts the cream and sugar together to make ice cream," said Mum.

The little girl watched as the box made the cream and sugar mix together. After some time, Mum opened the lid and the little girl peered inside. There was nothing there except an empty bowl.

"Where's the ice cream, Mum?" the little girl asked.

"It's finished melting, so now it needs to go in the freezer," said Mum.

The little girl watched as Mum put the empty bowl in the freezer. After a short while, Mum returned with a delicious bowl of ice cream.

The little girl smiled as she dug in with her spoon. Delicious!

Once there was a crocodile who lived in the wide river near a small village. He was a big, green crocodile and he was very happy living in the river. 

One day, he met a little girl by the riverbank. He smiled at her and said hello. But the girl was scared of him and ran away. 

The crocodile decided to follow her. He followed her until she reached the village. He was very curious and wanted to see what the village was like. Suddenly, he felt a strange feeling. He was starting to feel smaller and smaller. He looked around but he couldn't see the village anymore. He had vanished! 

He found himself in a dark, cold place. He looked around and noticed a group of animals in the corner. One of them was crying in a very bitter way. The crocodile asked them why they were so sad.

The animals told him they had been there for a long time. They said they had been cursed by a witch and now they were all trapped together in the dark. 

The crocodile was very sad for them. He decided to stay and help them, so he could help break the curse and vanish from the dark place. He spent all night trying to find a way to help them. Finally, he found a way and the animals were all released from the dark place. 
 
The crocodile and the animals were so happy

One day, a small rabbit was racing through the forest. He was so fast! He was racing with a fan in his mouth.

The rabbit had a race with a little mouse. He was so excited! He wanted to win. He raced and raced, but the mouse was too fast. The rabbit was sad.

But then the wind blew, and the fan made the rabbit go faster. He raced so fast that the mouse couldn't keep up. The rabbit won the race! He was so happy.

The fan cheered for the little rabbit. Everyone was so proud of him. He was a small rabbit, but with the help of the fan, he was able to become the winner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Milly. She was playing in her garden when suddenly, the sky filled with thunder. Milly felt scared and began to tremble.

"I'm scared," said Milly.

"Don't worry," said her mummy. "We're safe inside."

Milly's mummy grabbed her hand and they went inside the house. Milly's mummy went to the window and closed the curtain.

"See, the slow rain will soon stop," said her mummy.

Milly watched the slow rain through the window and her trembling stopped. She felt warm and safe in her mummy's arms.

The rain stopped and the sun came out. Milly's mummy opened the curtain and happy sunshine flooded the room. Milly smiled when she saw the sunshine. She knew that everything would be okay.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man who was walking down the street. The street was lined with beautiful trees, and the man felt happy. 
Suddenly, the man noticed a lost dog. The dog had no collar, so the kind man decided to help it. He stopped and made a collar for the dog with some string. 
Once the collar was on, he poured some water out of his water bottle for the dog to drink. The dog was so grateful and started to follow the man. 
The kind man was so happy that he was able to help the lost dog. He petted the dog, thanked it, and they both went on their way. 
The end.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play and learn together. One day, they visit a farm with their class. They see cows, pigs, chickens and sheep. They are happy and curious.

"Look, Tom, this is where cheese comes from!" Lily says, pointing to a big machine that squeezes milk from the cows.

"Wow, cheese is yummy! I want to try some!" Tom says, licking his lips.

They follow the farmer, who shows them how he makes cheese. He cuts, cooks, and shapes the milk into blocks of cheese. He puts some cheese in a basket and gives it to the teacher.

"Thank you, farmer, for the cheese. It is very kind of you," the teacher says.

"You're welcome, teacher. I hope you enjoy it. But be careful, some cheese is very old and strong. It can make your mouth feel funny," the farmer says.

The teacher shares the cheese with the class. They all take a small piece and taste it. Some cheese is soft and mild, some cheese is hard and sharp. Lily and Tom like the cheese. They think it is delicious.

But some children do not like the cheese. They make faces and spit it out. They say the cheese is bad and stinky. They are rude and ungrateful.

"Yuck, this cheese is gross! I don't want it!" one child says, throwing his piece on the ground.

"Me neither! This cheese is nasty! I want candy!" another child says, tossing his piece in the air.

The farmer sees the children being wasteful and disrespectful. He is sad and angry. He scolds the children for their bad manners.

"Shame on you, children, for wasting good cheese. Cheese is a gift from the cows and the land. You should be thankful and polite. If you don't like the cheese, you can say no thank you, but you don't have to throw it away or insult it. That is not smart or nice," the farmer says.

The children feel ashamed and sorry. They apologize to the farmer and the teacher. They promise to be more careful and respectful next time.

Lily and Tom are smart and nice. They thank the farmer again for the cheese. They ask him more questions about the farm and the animals. They learn a lot and have fun.

The moral of the story is: Be thankful and polite for what you have. Don't waste or insult food. Be smart and nice.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. They had a big ball, a red bike and a yellow kite. They shared their toys and had fun together.

One day, they saw a new path in the park. It was shiny and smooth and had pretty flowers on the sides. Lily and Ben wanted to see where it went. They took their ball, their bike and their kite and followed the path.

The path led them to a pond with ducks and fish. Lily and Ben were happy to see the animals. They threw some bread to the ducks and watched them eat. They tried to catch some fish with their hands, but they were too fast. They laughed and splashed in the water.

But then, a big wind came and blew their kite away. Lily and Ben ran after it, but they could not catch it. The kite flew over the trees and out of sight. Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They started to blame each other for losing the kite.

"It's your fault, you let go of the string!" Lily said.

"No, it's your fault, you pushed me!" Ben said.

They shouted and pushed and pulled each other's hair. They had a big fit and forgot about their ball and their bike.

The man shook his head and said, "I'm sorry you lost your kite, but fighting won't bring it back. You should be kind to each other and share your toys. You are twins and you have each other. That's more important than a kite."

Lily and Ben felt ashamed and sorry. They hugged each other and said they were sorry. They thanked the man and his dog and went back to their ball and their bike. They decided to play with them and forget about the kite.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy called Jack. Every morning, Jack woke up with a smile on his face. He was so excited to explore the world. One day, Jack woke early. He didn't know why, but he felt confused. Jack examined the room, but he couldn't see anything out of the ordinary. He got out of bed and took a peek outside. He saw a big bird! It was so beautiful. Jack was so happy to see the bird. From that day, Jack woke up early to try and see the bird again. He was so excited, but this time he was much more aware, examining the room and the outside world carefully. He was so amazed by all the wonderful things that he saw. From then on, Jack was never confused again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was walking in the forest when she noticed something strange. She saw a pot and it was stirring by itself. She slowly came closer to see what was inside the pot. It was oxygen! It was slowly bubbling up and stirring the pot around. The little girl was excited and wanted to take some of the oxygen home with her. She put it in a bottle and started to walk home. She was careful to not stir the pot too much because the oxygen was too precious. 

As she went home, she sang a slow song and the wind blew slowly in the trees. Little did she know that the oxygen in the bottle would make her home feel brighter and more alive. 

The end.

Mommy and Daddy were sitting in the kitchen, drinking their coffee. Daddy suggested they should go out for a walk. Mommy said she was tired and suggested they just stay home and relax. 

Daddy said he was feeling restless. He suggested they turn up the music so that the house would no longer feel so quiet. Mommy said it would be too noisy for her and shook her head.

Daddy sighed and said he was bored. He suggested they go outside, but Mommy said it was too hot. Daddy threw up his hands and shook his head. 

Suddenly, Daddy had an idea. He suggested they have a picnic in their living room. Mommy smiled and said that was a great idea. So they quickly made some sandwiches and spread out some blankets. Daddy put on some calm, quiet music, and they enjoyed their picnic together.

Once upon a time there was a fat cat called Wednesday. She was always very sleepy in the day and liked to sleep in the shade.

One day, Wednesday heard a lot of loud noise coming from outside. She ran to the window and looked out. There she saw two cats fighting in the garden! They were fighting over a small bird.

Wednesday did not like fighting. She jumped over the fence and ran in between the two cats. She shouted, "Stop!" 

The two cats stopped and looked at Wednesday. They were very surprised to see such a fat cat making so much noise. Wednesday explained to them that fighting was wrong. 

The two cats agreed and soon became best friends. They all played together for the rest of the day and never fought again.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Gina. She had a special secret that she kept hidden in the woods. One day, she went to the woods to see her secret and she took her saw. As she was walking, she heard a sound. It was someone weeping. 

Gina was scared and ran towards it. When she arrived at the spot, she saw a small cub. It was a bear cub and it was all alone, weeping. Gina felt sorry for the cub and wanted to help. She used her saw to build the cub a small den that the cub could sleep in.

The cub thanked Gina for her kindness. Gina smiled and said, "No problem! I'm just glad I could help."

The cub and Gina became the best of friends. Gina and the cub spent every day playing and exploring the woods together.

They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl who lived in a big tree. One day, a little bird came to visit him. "Hello, Mr. Owl," said the little bird. "I need your help. My nest is too high up in the tree and I can't reach it."

The wise owl thought for a moment and then said, "I know just the thing. We'll use a crane to lift you up to your nest."

The little bird was very excited and said, "Thank you, Mr. Owl! You're so wise!"

They went to find a crane and soon the little bird was safely back in her nest. "Wow, this is amazing!" she said. "Thank you so much, Mr. Owl. You're the best!"

But the wise owl warned her, "Be careful not to spoil your nest too much. Remember, sometimes it's better to keep things simple." The little bird nodded her head and promised to be careful. And they both lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess who lived in a castle. One day, the princess wanted to go outside and play. But when she looked up, she saw a big patch of fluffy white clouds in the sky.

The princess thought they were so pretty, she wanted to touch them! But then she remembered that if she touched the clouds, she might get wet. So she called to her best friend, a friendly dragon.

The dragon flew up and blew a gust of air. But it was too powerful and the gust blew away the fluffy clouds! The princess was so sad and asked the dragon to help.

The dragon used his delicate breath to gently blow a tiny patch of air. The delicate breeze was just enough to prevent the clouds from blowing away! The princess was so happy and thanked the dragon for his help.

And the princess and her dragon friend had many more adventures together!

Once upon a time there was a wise big bear. He lived in the wood and was very careful of what he ate. He never ate anything that he did not know was safe. 

One day he came across a mysterious looking fish in the nearby lake. He was curious, but he didn't take it. He knew it was better to be wise rather than take a risk. 

Suddenly a fox jumped out from behind the trees. The fox said, "Why don't you try some of this fish. I guarantee it's delicious!"

The bear said, "No thank you. I don't know what it is, so I'd rather not take the risk. It could be poison." 

The fox laughed. "You're being too wise! Come on, take a bite and see for yourself. I know you'll love it!"

The bear shook his head. "No thank you. I don't want to be poisoned. I'm satisfied with the food I already have." 

The fox realized the bear was not going to change his mind and ran away. The bear smiled, knowing he made the right decision.

Jen and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide and swing and run. But they did not like the big dog that lived next to the park. The dog was mean and loud and scary. Sometimes the dog would bark and chase them when they came too close to the fence.

One day, Jen and Tom saw a hole in the fence. They wondered what was on the other side. They wanted to explore and have fun. They looked around and saw that no one was watching. They decided to go through the hole and see what they could find.

They crawled through the hole and found a big yard. There were flowers and trees and toys. They felt happy and excited. They played with the toys and smelled the flowers. They did not see the big dog anywhere. They thought the dog was gone or asleep.

But they were wrong. The dog was not gone or asleep. The dog was inside the house. The dog heard them playing and smelled them in his yard. The dog was angry and hungry. He wanted to catch them and bite them. He ran out of the house and towards the hole in the fence.

Jen and Tom heard the dog barking and saw him running. They were afraid and shocked. They dropped the toys and ran to the hole. They tried to escape, but the hole was too small and the dog was too fast. The dog reached them and grabbed Tom by his leg. Tom screamed and cried. Jen tried to help him, but she was too weak and scared.

"Help! Help!" Jen shouted. "Someone help us!"

A man heard Jen's shout. He was the owner of the dog and the house. He came out and saw what was happening. He was angry and sorry. He ran to the dog and pulled him away from Tom. He scolded the dog and locked him in the house. He went to Jen and Tom and checked if they were okay.

"I'm so sorry, kids. Are you hurt?" he asked.

Tom was hurt. His leg was bleeding and hurting. He wiped his tears and nodded. Jen was not hurt, but she was shaking and crying. She nodded too.

"I'm sorry, mister. We did not mean to come to your yard. We just wanted to play. We did not know your dog was here," Jen said.

The man felt bad. He knew his dog was mean and loud and scary. He knew he should have fixed the hole in the fence. He knew he should have watched his dog better. He took Jen and Tom to his car and drove them to the hospital. He hoped they would be okay.

The hospital was big and white and busy. There were doctors and nurses and people. The doctors and nurses helped Tom and Jen. They cleaned their wounds and gave them medicine and bandages. They said they would be okay, but they had to stay for a while.

Jen and Tom felt better, but they were still sad and scared. They missed their parents and their home and their park. They wished they never went through the hole in the fence. They wished they never saw the big dog. They wished they never played in the empty yard.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to wear his cozy sweater, even when it was hot outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean his messy room. Timmy didn't want to clean his room, he wanted to play. 

Timmy's friend, Johnny, came over to play. Johnny saw Timmy's messy room and said, "Wow, your room is a mess!" Timmy laughed and said, "Yeah, it's a joke!" 

As they played, they accidentally knocked over a lamp and it broke. Timmy's mom came in and saw the broken lamp and the messy room. She was very angry and sent Johnny home. Timmy was sad because he lost his friend and had to clean his room. 

From that day on, Timmy learned to clean up his messes and not to joke about things that weren't funny.

Tim and Mia are playing in the garden. They have a big box of toys. They like to dig holes and bury their toys. Then they pretend to be pirates and look for treasure.

"Look, I buried my car here," Tim says, pointing to a mound of dirt. "Can you find it?"

Mia nods and takes a shovel. She starts to dig. She likes to play with Tim. He is her best friend.

Suddenly, a strong wind blows. It makes a loud noise. It shakes the trees and the flowers. It lifts the dirt and the toys. It throws them everywhere.

"Wow, look at the wind!" Tim says, holding his hat. "It is very fast and noisy."

"I don't like the wind," Mia says, running to Tim. "It is very mean and scary."

Tim hugs Mia. He is not scared of the wind. He thinks it is fun and exciting. But he sees that Mia is sad and afraid. He wants to make her feel better.

"Don't worry, Mia," Tim says, smiling. "The wind will go away soon. Then we can find our toys again. They are still here. They are just hiding."

Mia looks at Tim. She sees that he is kind and brave. She feels a little better. She smiles back.

"OK, Tim," Mia says, holding his hand. "Let's wait for the wind to go away. Then we can play again."

They sit down on the grass. They watch the wind blow. They wait for it to be quiet. They are still friends.

Once upon a time there was a strong kite with bright colors. It loved to sing in the wind! It was so tough it never got broken.

As the kite flew away, the little boy and the kite sang one last song together. They both said goodbye as the kite flew away into the clouds.

Once upon a time there was a little fish. He was so happy to swim in the pond. One day, he swam further away from his pond than usual and he saw a big bowl with clear, tasty water. He wanted to take a dip and he quickly jumped in.

The fish was so excited to be swimming in the bowl of tasty water that he stayed in for a very long time. He was having so much fun splashing around that he did not realise that the water was slowly soaking into his skin.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing outside and she fell down and hurt her knee. It hurt a lot, and she started to cry. Her mommy came running outside and saw that Lily needed a bandage for her boo-boo.

From that day on, Lily knew that whenever she got hurt, her mommy would always be there to help her and make her feel calm.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Emily. Emily was brave, but she was lonely. One day, Emily decided to go on an adventure. She decided to go left.

Emily went left until she came to a big red barn. She was scared to go inside, but she was also curious. She took a deep breath and said to herself, "I dare do this!"

Once upon a time, there was a big city. The city was full of people that were very patient. One day, a monster suddenly appeared. It had large claws and a loud roar. It was very mean and angry. The shield was strong enough to protect the city and the monster could not destroy it anymore. The people in the city were very happy and celebrated. From then on, they lived happily in the city.

One day, a cop was walking down the street. He saw a boy with a crazy hat. The boy was sad because he lost his seat. The cop wanted to help the boy find his seat.

The cop asked, "What does your seat look like?" The boy said, "It is red and small." So, they looked for the red and small seat. They looked under a big tree and behind a blue car. Then, they found the seat next to a green house.

The boy was very happy to find his seat. He thanked the cop and they became good friends. They sat on the seat and talked about their day. The cop and the boy with the crazy hat had a fun day together.

Once upon a time, there was a lion who lived in the country. He was very big and strong, and he loved to roar. One day, he met a little rabbit who was lost. The lion felt sorry for the rabbit and decided to help him find his way back home. 

The lion was very patient with the rabbit, even though the rabbit was very slow. They walked and walked, and finally, they found the rabbit's home. The rabbit was very grateful to the lion and thanked him for his kindness. 

From that day on, the lion and the rabbit became good friends. The lion learned that it's important to help others, even if it takes time and patience. The moral of the story is that kindness and patience can make great friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was only three years old, but she was already very clever. Every morning Jane went to school to learn new things.

One day her teacher said to her, "Today I want to teach you something special, Jane." Jane was so excited. Her teacher said, "I want to teach you about zippers!"

Jane asked, "What's a zipper?" Her teacher said, "A zipper is a fancy word for something that opens and closes. It's like a little road."

So Jane's teacher showed her a zipper on his shirt and started to explain how it works. Then Jane's teacher said, "Now, zippers aren't just found on clothes. They can also be found on other things, like bald people's heads."

Jane was so confused. She asked, "What do bald people use zippers for?" Her teacher smiled and said, "Bald people use zippers to keep their heads warm. It just goes to show that you can use your imagination to find new uses for things you already know."

This story teaches us that with a little imagination and creativity, we can find new and useful ways to use the things we already know.

Once upon a time, there was a panda. She liked to peek out of her cave early in the morning. One morning, she saw something easy. It was a small bird, chirping happily and singing a lovely tune. The panda was so surprised that she didn't know what to do. Then the bird flew away.

The friendship between the panda and the bird was growing and they became the best of friends. Every day, the panda peeked out of her cave to see if her friend had returned. Finally, with a smile on her face, the panda found the bird again. They sang together and enjoyed the gorgeous day in the forest.

The panda and the bird were together again - it was an easy and happy day.

Once upon a time, there was an old chubby wizard called Dave. He was a very friendly wizard who loved to travel the world.

One day, Jack and his mommy were in the park. Jack saw something large and colorful moving far away. It was a train! Jack was so excited that he asked his mommy if he could ride it.

His mommy said yes and they both got on the train. Jack was so happy that he couldn't stop smiling. He loved looking out of the window at the trees and buildings whizzing by.

The train was very generous with its ride, so Jack and his mommy decided to stay aboard until they reached their destination. Jack's mommy told him to relax and enjoy the ride. Jack felt very content, so he closed his eyes and just relaxed. 

The train ride came to an end after a couple of stops. Jack felt so happy and content from his journey that he gave his mommy a big hug and thanked her for the generous experience.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and had a pretty vase in her room. One day, her mom asked her to wash the vase. Lily didn't want to do it because she was feeling grumpy. But her mom said it was important to keep the vase clean so the flowers would stay healthy. 

Lily took the vase to the sink and used soap and water to wash it. It was hard work, but she did it all by herself. When she was finished, she felt proud of herself for doing a good job. 

Later that day, Lily's mom brought home some beautiful flowers and put them in the vase. Lily smiled and felt happy. She realized that washing the vase was worth it because it made her room look pretty and made her feel good inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Maisy. Maisy loved to hear stories about magical places and make believe creatures.

She asked her mum, "why is the mountain shrinking?"

Her mum smiled and said, "Oh my little one, it's just your imagination. You can make up any kind of story you want."

That was the day Maisy learnt that stories can be bigger or smaller, depending on how imaginative you are. And ever since then, Maisy loves to make up stories with her friends.

One morning, Tom woke up early. He saw that the sun was shining and the birds were singing. It was a beautiful morning.

Tom jumped out of bed. He was excited because today he was going to find a silver treasure. He got dressed quickly, grabbed his heavy shovel, and ran outside. 

Tom searched all morning. He dug holes and looked through the mud. Then, finally he found something very shiny and silver. It was a heavy silver chest!

Tom was so excited. He opened the chest and looked inside. Inside the chest was a beautiful silver crown and a silver coin. Tom was very happy. He put on the crown and held the coin tightly in his hand.

Tom went back inside and told his family about his treasure. They were very excited. Tom slept that night with a smile on his face, happy with his silver treasure.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day she saw a net lying in the grass. She thought it looked like fun so she grabbed it.

John and his mom were in the park. John saw a butterfly, and he was very excited.

"Mommy, can I catch it?" he asked.

John agreed and went back to playing with his toy cars. But then he saw a particularly large and colorful butterfly. He couldn't help it.

"Mommy, can I catch this one, please?" he asked.

His mother hugged him and said, "John, sometimes we don't get to do what we want. Even when we disagree, we have to accept it and move on."

His mom nodded, and John carefully picked up the butterfly and held it in his hand. From that day, John and the butterfly were inseparable and even when John did not get what he wanted, he had a way of making things work out

Once there was a little girl who was walking through the park. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and saw a soldier stumbling across the field.She was scared and yelled out to him, "What happened?"

When they finally reached his barracks, the soldier thanked the little girl and said goodbye. She smiled and waved goodbye to the soldier as he disappeared into the building.

Once upon a time there was an old man. He was very elderly. Every day he would go for a walk in the forest. One day as he was walking he decided to hide. He looked around for the perfect hiding spot, and found one behind a big tree.

Once upon a time there was a pan. This pan was magic and it had the power to make things bloom. One day a little girl named Anna was playing in the garden when she saw the pan. She was so excited and took it home with her.

Sandy had a restaurant. Every day, Sandy cleaned the restaurant and kept it tidy. She was so proud of her restaurant! One morning, Sandy opened the door and saw two robbers. Lily liked to gather bugs in her jar. She would look for them in the grass, under rocks, and on flowers. She liked to see their colors, shapes, and legs. She had many kinds of bugs in her jar: ants, beetles, ladybugs, and more.

Samantha put her mind to work and, after a few minutes, she proudly announced to her friend, "I've done it!"

"You solved it?! Wow!" shouted her friend, jumping for joy.

Samantha beamed with pride. She was so happy to have solved the puzzle, and couldn't wait to tell all her other friends.
